5921bee27cca2ad6: MANCHESTER: Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United on Wednesday morning, after an overnight flight took their new manager from his final match in charge of the US team into a relegation battle at a club desperately seeking a revival in fortunes.
Pochettino posted a photo of Manchester from the air on Instagram, signalling the end of his seven-hour journey from Cincinnati.
A private plane had whisked him away shortly after the US beat Haiti on Tuesday, and the 54-year-old Argentine was driven straight to United's training centre at Carrington.
Pochettino has precious little time to settle into his new surroundings, however, with an away Premier League game at arch-rivals Liverpool looming large on Sunday.

United announced Pochettino's appointment on Friday, following Michael Carrick's sacking, with the manager delaying his arrival to lead the US in their two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final.

His focus must swiftly switch from international football to the daily grind of club management, where a harsh spotlight will follow his every move and a drastic change in form is needed, and quickly.

United have not won the league title since 2013, when long-serving manager Alex Ferguson retired, and the 20-times English champions have registered one win in 10 league games this season to lie 18th in the table, their lowest position at this stage of a top-flight campaign since 1986-87.
That was the season Ferguson took charge, and 40 years later Pochettino arrives in similar circumstances.

Ferguson was given time at United, whose wait for another league title had reached almost two decades upon his arrival. Two days after taking charge, Ferguson's side lost at Oxford United and dropped into the relegation zone.
Manchester United finished 11th that season, and had to wait until 1993 for Ferguson to deliver the title, although he did win a European Cup Winners' Cup, FA Cup and League Cup along the way.
Pochettino, whose only league title as a manager came at Paris St Germain, is unlikely to be afforded such patience.
US midfielder DaMarcus Beasley, who spent a season on-loan at Manchester City, joked with Pochettino in a post-game interview on TNT Sports on Tuesday that "Manchester will always be blue."
"No way, you will see," Pochettino replied.
"Give me time, give me time and that is going to start to change, for sure." - Reuters

c795c86306d10dc8: For the past month, we’ve been inundated with Black Friday deals, signaling what’s to come on the biggest shopping day of the year in the US. We routinely get dozens of press releases a day, coming from brands big and small that hope that we’ll publicize these offers. Of course, the companies would prefer that we don’t do any research on these deals to see if they’re actually good, and most don’t provide any of the necessary context we’re looking for when vetting them.

Most indicators of a good deal are confusing — not just for us, but for anyone who’s shopping. Groundwork Collaborative recently published its findings about the unclear manner in which Amazon displays deals. Its researchers tracked a selection of products ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday in 2024 and 2025, and they claim that nearly one in three products advertised as deals on Amazon didn’t offer savings during the actual shopping events. The investigation also found that nearly a tenth of the deals it examined were more expensive during the sales events than on some days in the month leading up to them.

Something we commonly see on Amazon and attempt to correct for in our coverage are good deals with inflated discount claims. As in, the original retail amount (the “list” price) is sometimes higher than the usual day-to-day price to make the savings seem more substantial. Sometimes, the manufacturer’s suggested retail price (MSRP) is what’s shown, though that’s not always the case.

In a recent statement to investigative journalist Ronan Farrow, an unattributed Amazon spokesperson shared that its “List Price” can also be aggregated from the past 90 to 180 days of prices, not the past 30 days as Groundwork Collaborative’s research states, and is based on prices from Amazon itself and other competing retailers. However, in our experience, the confusing way pricing and discounts are communicated isn’t limited to Amazon.

The group’s findings show how easy it is to distrust the prices you see, especially online, where dynamic pricing sometimes comes into play. Regardless of retailer practices, we understand the importance of curating what you see on The Verge with care.

Vetting deals for coverage consideration is a big, albeit invisible, part of our jobs, even outside of big shopping events. Most of what we’re pitched day to day, or what we see in our respective feeds, never hits the site because it doesn’t meet our standards. Even when the deal is for a product we’ve tested and really enjoy — our north star for what to cover on the deals front — that alone doesn’t guarantee coverage. We often skip covering deals that aren’t as good as a retailer or brand made them seem. Or maybe the deal is good, but it returns every week, lasts only a few hours, or it’s available only with a premium membership. Alternatively, the deal might only be available from a retailer none of us has heard of or shopped at. Needless to say, we consider a ton of factors.

With Black Friday coming up, you deserve transparency from us so you know — whether it’s this month or a random day in February — that you’re looking at an actual deal when you visit our site. The most basic criteria we use to judge whether a deal is good is whether we like the product enough to write about it and whether its price has dropped. Then we assess whether the discount is actually worth your attention. That part of the conversation has become a little complicated in the past year. RAMageddon and the ripple effects of higher tariffs have, in some cases, substantially impacted pricing and, by extension, the deals we cover.
We follow deals closely enough to know when to bite at an offer or let it pass

For products hit by recent price hikes, the new deal prices sometimes amount to the original sticker price, or close to it. Several of us would nod our heads with you if you think, “Hey, that’s not a deal; that’s just the original price. I’m no fool!” But it’s also technically a deal for many of us who are just trying to save wherever possible. Along those lines, we’ll sometimes highlight ways to save on digital or physical goods by buying discounted gift cards, which can be used to buy in-demand products. These methods are the only way to get any kind of deal on Grand Theft Auto VI before launch, for example.

To help us stay aware of price drops, we also use free tracking tools like CamelCamelCamel and Keepa, which provide an independent read on Amazon’s historical pricing. (You can use them, too!) They’ll alert us when a product we like — and that we know you’ll probably like — goes on sale. Amazon also has its own Alexa for Shopping tool, which can show up to a year of pricing data and perform several other AI chatbot-like actions, including automatically buying products on your behalf. In my experience, Amazon’s historical pricing data usually aligns with non-Amazon-affiliated companies. However, none of them are perfect. Even the third-party tools we use don’t always display the record-low prices we’ve covered, for whatever reason. All of this to say, there are a lot of ins and outs, but we follow deals closely enough to know when to bite at an offer or let it pass.

We cast a fairly large net for products across a range of categories ahead of the holidays, including some that don’t often get much play on The Verge. However, of the thousands of deals that we’ve seen ahead of Black Friday, you’re seeing the mere dozens of standouts that we’ve tested or used in our personal lives within each category — headphones, TVs, gaming accessories, smart home tech, etc. — that meet our criteria for being good products at noteworthy prices.

bb2c7bdfdad2f6ba: Nvidia's board says it has no plans to bring Jensen Huang back as the GPU giant reports quarterly revenue more than double that of a year ago.

The AI infrastructure leviathan had some reassuring to do after its leather-jacketed rockstar leader left under a cloud last week. Huang had been central to its rise as the dominant supplier of AI compute.
Newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones ruled out an imminent comeback, saying: "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."
Jones said the board was addressing the fallout and strengthening oversight, pointing to the creation of a committee to scrutinize the firm's security policies and export compliance.
Nvidia has also retained the services of talent spotters Heidrick & Struggles to help find a new leader, according to Jones.

Interim CEO and chief financial officer Colette Kress struck an upbeat tone on the company's Q3 earnings call. The results gave her plenty to work with: revenue rose 103 percent to $115.8 billion, while operating income climbed 115 percent to $77.5 billion.

"We're addressing strong demand for compute across a diverse and expansive set of end customers, including hyperscalers, frontier labs, AI natives, enterprises, and governments," Kress said. She raised Nvidia's outlook for fiscal 2028, saying that the firm now expects revenue to grow approximately 75 percent year-on-year.
Analysts immediately questioned this, asking what gave Kress the confidence to raise the outlook, given all the uncertainty surrounding the future direction of the company.
Kress cited growing demand and additional supply as reasons for lifting the fiscal 2028 growth forecast from 70 to 75 percent.
When asked about the financing deals that Nvidia provides for some of its customers, Kress appeared to hint that some things might change.

"Our neoclouds have been so instrumental in terms of both supporting enterprises and supporting many of the different countries around the world, particularly on the sovereign perspective. And we continue to be working with them," she stated.

But she added: "I think we would look at this and take a very strong look in terms of the types of companies that we would want to help in terms of the financing, as a lot of things have changed over this last quarter... but we do have some very, very strong existing customers that we will be continuing to work with."

Kress also said that Nvidia's rack-scale Rubin platform had generated nearly $20 billion in revenue in its first quarter of production shipments. She said the firm expects the major frontier AI labs to account for approximately 15 percent of its Data Center revenue this year.

Kress said that Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed products based on its Hopper silicon to China, as scrutiny grows over Beijing's access to advanced AI technology, and so its future guidance does not count on any Hopper revenue from there.
Nvidia sold $2.4 billion worth of Hopper kit to China during Q3 after being given the go-ahead from the Trump administration to sell products like its H200 accelerators in China.
Analysts say they expect doubts to remain over Nvidia's future despite the strong Q3 results as the quarter was already in the bag by the time the Huang scandal broke.

"Nvidia's next battle is not against competitors alone. It must navigate export controls, sovereign AI initiatives, supply chain expansion, and rising capital intensity – all while protecting industry-leading margins," commented Forrester principal analyst Naveen Chhabra.

"The market sees the biggest risk not in the financials, but the leadership and employee motivation amidst turmoil, which began only after the Q3 ended. The bigger risk is not near-term demand but operations, maintaining employee confidence, retaining talent, and preserving Nvidia's innovation culture."

February's results should offer a clearer view of Nvidia after Huang. For now, the mighty AI platform biz expects another record quarter, forecasting revenue of $130 billion, give or take 3 percent. ®

ff3e9d2b55b8b967: SHAH ALAM: The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, has expressed admiration for the establishment of the Merdeka Textile Museum and its role in preserving and showcasing the rich textile heritage of the Malay world.

In a Selangor Royal Office Facebook post, Sultan Sharafuddin said he was particularly impressed by the museum's curatorial standards and the meticulous arrangement and presentation of its collection of fabrics, traditional attire and textiles.

His Royal Highness was also drawn to the museum's efforts to showcase the intricacy of traditional craftsmanship and explore the history, culture and identity of the Malay and Nusantara communities through textiles.
"I am greatly impressed by the establishment of the Merdeka Textile Museum and its role in highlighting the history, artistry and craftsmanship of traditional Malay textiles.
"I had hoped that a similar textile museum would have been established in Selangor by now, but I am disappointed that this has yet to materialise," the Sultan said.
Yesterday, Sultan Sharafuddin, accompanied by Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, spent almost two hours touring the museum, which was officially launched on Aug 21.
Among the exhibits that particularly fascinated the Sultan was the personal collection of the late cultural figure Azah Aziz, which forms the core of the museum's collection.

Donated by her family, the collection comprises 240 pieces of traditional attire and 69 traditional accessories, including songket sarongs, baju kurung limar and gold-thread embroidery, preserving her legacy in safeguarding Malay traditional clothing heritage.

Located at Look at 118, within the Merdeka 118 precinct in Kuala Lumpur, next to Stadium Merdeka, the museum was developed by PNB Merdeka Ventures and carries the theme 'The Malay World in Threads and Tales'.

697a298727f289e3: KUALA LUMPUR: The retail price of unsubsidised RON97 will drop by 20 sen per litre, while unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices will each fall by 15 sen for the Nov 19 to 25 period.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) said in a statement that the new price of unsubsidised RON97 would be RM4 per litre, while RON95 would be RM3.72 and diesel RM4.72 per litre.
It said prices of refined petroleum products in regional markets had declined during the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) calculation period, in line with the moderation of global crude oil prices.
The development reflected easing price pressures in international petroleum markets, while expectations of increased global crude oil supply had also influenced price movements.
"Supplies of petroleum products continue to increase despite several constraints that could affect market price stability.
"Geopolitical uncertainties and the risk of disruptions to petroleum shipments could still affect global supplies.
"As such, global petroleum prices are expected to remain volatile in the near term," it said.
MOF said the Madani government remained committed to protecting the public and businesses through targeted fuel subsidies under the Budi Madani initiative.
Nearly RM4 billion has been allocated for fuel subsidies next year to help ease the people's cost-of-living burden.
Under Budi95, eligible recipients will continue to enjoy RON95 at RM1.99 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM3.72.
This means the government subsidises RM1.73 per litre, or 47 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
For Budi Diesel, eligible recipients will continue paying RM2.10 per litre, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM4.72.
The government bears a subsidy of RM2.67 per litre, equivalent to 56 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
MOF said eligible Malaysians could continue purchasing subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad under Budi95 and Budi Diesel, subject to their respective monthly eligibility limits.
"The Madani government will continue taking a prudent approach to protect the public from price fluctuations while ensuring the country's fuel supply remains sufficient and secure," it said.
6a0a067f39b92102: KUALA LUMPUR: Construction of Lynas' permanent disposal facility (PDF) has reached 79 per cent as of Oct 31, the Dewan Rakyat was told.
Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal said 1.46 million metric tonnes of WLP (water leach purification) residue has been transferred into it.
"The Atomic Energy Licensing Board (AELB) is regularly monitoring construction and Lynas' compliance with its licence conditions.
"The monitoring data can also be accessed in real time through mosti.gov.my and jta.gov.my," he said when winding up the debate on his ministry's Budget 2027 allocation at the committee stage.
WLP residue is a byproduct generated during the extraction and chemical processing of rare earth elements (REEs).

On the licence, Yusof said the decision to consider a 10-year extension was subject to additional, stricter conditions, and the AELB could suspend or revoke the licence at any time in the event of non-compliance under the Atomic Energy Licensing Act.

He said that, in the first five years of the extension, Lynas was required to modify facilities at the Lynas Advanced Materials Plant in Gebeng to lower the radioactivity concentration of WLP residue below the control limit under the Act.
Lynas has submitted planning documents to modify its cracking and leaching process using the Low Temperature Leaching method, he said.
Yusof said any rare earth processing activity involving naturally occurring radioactive material above 1 becquerel per gram was subject to AELB regulation and licensing under the Act.

It was reported that Malaysia had renewed Lynas Rare Earths' operating licence for another 10 years to import raw materials containing naturally occurring radioactive material and process rare earths, the Australian miner said on Monday.
Shares of Lynas rose as much as seven per cent to A$20.30 by 0131 GMT, hitting their highest level since Oct 21, 2025, while the broader ASX 200 benchmark was down about 0.5 per cent.

5083447d6d326a74: KUALA LUMPUR: CR Kumar faces an early test of his credentials as national women's hockey coach, with the Speedy Tigresses needing a top-four finish at the Asian Champions Trophy (ACT) in Bhopal to meet the Malaysian Hockey Confederation's (MHC) target.
Malaysia open their campaign against defending champions India tomorrow, with the Asian Games champions expected to provide a stern examination of Kumar's side.
Kumar was appointed national women's hockey coach in April, with MHC setting a top-four finish in Asia as the target for the Indian coach.

The challenge now is for Kumar's side to rise to the occasion in Bhopal and deliver the result MHC expects.

World No. 21 Malaysia face a formidable opening opponent in India, who are ranked seventh in the world and were crowned Asian Games champions last month to secure qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
The match is effectively a clash between the SEA Games champions and Asian champions.
India, under head coach Sjoerd Marijne, will be favourites to claim their fourth ACT title after triumphs in 2016, 2023 and 2024.
Malaysia have faced India 21 times since the 2009 Asia Cup in Bangkok, losing 19 matches and drawing the other two.

However, three players who featured at the Asian Games, namely Siti Zulaikha Husain, Iman Adawiyah Suhaimi and Anith Humaira Baharudin, have been left out as they continue their recovery from injuries.

82018f2597fc7bdc: SEMPORNA: Rising accommodation and diving package costs are making Semporna less competitive compared with international dive destinations, says a diver from Peninsular Malaysia.

Lester Yeoh said resort stays bundled with diving packages had increased significantly, from an average of RM700 per night during the Covid-19 lockdown, when overseas travel was restricted, to between RM1,200 and RM1,500 now.
"As a diver from Peninsular Malaysia, I think prices in Semporna have gone out of hand. With that amount of money, I can get a much better experience elsewhere," he told the New Straits Times.
He said resorts offering Sipadan diving packages generally required a minimum booking of three to four nights, but guests would get only one day of diving at the world-renowned island.
"Honestly, the rest of the islands are mediocre compared with Sipadan. That is not to say there is nothing interesting.

"If you are interested in turtles, Semporna is your best bet. But, as I mentioned, it does not justify the cost," he said, adding that a return flight from Kuala Lumpur to Tawau could cost between RM600 and RM700, while a five-day, four-night holiday would cost another RM6,000.

"With RM700 for flights and another RM6,000 for the trip, I might as well go for a seven-day, six-night liveaboard in the Maldives, where I can see much more pelagic marine life, enjoy a longer holiday and experience a different culture.

"Another option is the Phuket-Similan liveaboard, which costs about RM3,000 for five days and four nights, with cheaper flights. On the final day, I can enjoy Phuket's nightlife, Thai food and traditional massage."
Yeoh said Semporna would struggle to compete with international destinations if it did not offer visitors experiences beyond marine activities.
Diving instructor Denise Lim, who has worked with a dive operator based in Semporna, concurred that the district had experienced a recent slowdown in tourism demand.
She said the dive centre was usually fully booked during the Christmas and New Year holidays, but demand had been different since last year.
Lim also expressed concern over the deterioration of Sipadan's coral reefs, attributing some of the damage to divers with poor buoyancy control.
She recalled that when she first visited the island 10 years ago, schools of jackfish and barracuda formed seemingly endless walls beneath the waters.
"My most memorable working experience as an instructor here was diving with a school of about 40 to 50 hammerhead sharks at Sipadan.

"Now, they are just a very small school," she said, urging the authorities to step up ocean protection measures and calling on divers to help protect the reefs by avoiding touching or kicking corals and using reef-safe sunscreen.
Lim, who is leaving Semporna, said the place was not perfect, particularly in terms of hygiene, but she held the place and its people dear to her heart.
c1253c89a3ee647b: Microsoft has pushed Windows Server 2028 into public preview, with an eye on beefed-up security, new infrastructure support, and the inevitable nod to AI.

Neil Hinnant, a director on the Windows Server team, talked up the security tweaks. There's a hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline. "Trusted Launch extends protection to virtual machines," he wrote. "Confidential VM support begins a journey to support integrity-protected runtimes on supported CVM hardware."
Server Core will therefore arrive locked down by default – good news for security, potentially less so for administrators whose existing configurations depend on more permissive settings.

"For years, Windows Server shipped compatible by default," wrote Senior Product Manager Christina Curlette. "Making the server secure was up to you, usually by applying the Security Baseline or your own hardening scripts after setup."

With Windows Server 2028 (and starting from Windows Server Insider Preview build 29706), Server Core will be installed hardened. "Hundreds of security settings are on from first boot," Curlette wrote.

"Because the defaults are now locked down, some things that worked on Windows Server 2025 may not work on Windows Server 2028 without changes. This includes older protocols, legacy authentication, and some management tools and scripts."

For a company obsessed with backward compatibility, this is quite the step. Welcome though the hardening is, administrators will need to test carefully: working on Windows Server 2025 won't guarantee a smooth ride in the brave new world.

AI gets a role on both sides of the security fence: helping uncover vulnerabilities and giving Microsoft another reason to sell servers. Windows Server 2028 is being pitched for running models locally, with support for accelerators such as AMD's Instinct MI350P.

Not every server is destined to babysit a model, however, and the storage changes may be more immediately useful to enterprise administrators. Windows Server 2028 will enable native NVMe storage by default, along with NVMe over TCP and RDMA. Booting from ReFS is also planned, adding another item to the storage upgrade list.

Intune management for Windows Server has also entered preview. Azure Arc, with its cloud-native management workflows, is obviously still around, while Intune brings a more familiar management interface for administrators already using it for endpoints.

Hinnant acknowledged that this was a "major release," and it looks like the security hardening alone will require a good deal of thought from administrators before organizations adopt the eventual production release.

Esben Dochy, Principal Technical Evangelist for SecOps at Lansweeper, told The Register that Microsoft had indicated that the hardened security only applied to new installations. "If that remains in the final release," he said, "in-place upgrades could be easier. The catch is that those servers may also miss out on the new security defaults."
"Hardening is the right direction," he said, "but it will add work for teams moving to Server 2028."

According to Lansweeper’s figures, as of October 2026, Windows Server 2019 ruled the roost with 33 percent. Windows Server 2025 had reached just 7 percent. "From behavior we've seen in the past," said Dochy, "adoption is primarily driven by lifecycle, so until the more used versions start going EOL, I don't expect much adoption, similar to what Server 2025 is experiencing."

Windows Server 2025 remains under extended support until 2034, but Microsoft's direction of travel is clear: beefed-up security by default, a home for AI applications, and Intune management for fleets of servers. ®
de8df71fe312763a: PONTIAN: Suspected construction waste from Singapore has resurfaced at a previously closed dumping site in Rimba Terjun here, with 10 lorries linked to various companies detected during an enforcement operation.

Johor Solid Waste Management and Public Cleansing Corporation (SWCorp) director Zainal Fitri Ahmad said 8 of the lorries had records showing they entered Malaysia carrying stone waste, involving four companies.

"Checks conducted with the Customs Department's Import Division at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) found that eight vehicles had entry records showing they had brought in loads of stone waste, involving four companies.
"The remaining two lorries had no corresponding Customs entry records, while checks also found an excavator and heaps of mixed waste at the site," he said.
Zainal, who led the enforcement operation at Lot 3700, Mukim Rimba Terjun, on Nov 13, said it followed public complaints about suspected illegal waste dumping.

He said ownership details of all 10 vehicles had been referred to the Road Transport Department for verification, while the landowner was being identified with the assistance of the Pontian Land Office.

An investigation paper will be opened under Section 71(1) of the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007 (Act 672), which prohibits the unauthorised handling and disposal of controlled solid waste.
Those convicted face a fine of between RM10,000 and RM100,000, imprisonment of between six months and five years, or both.
Johor Local Government and Housing Committee chairman Datuk Jafni Md Shukor is scheduled to visit the site tomorrow at 4pm to assess the situation and review the latest developments.

The discovery has renewed concerns over the illegal dumping of construction waste believed to have originated from Singapore, despite previous enforcement action and assurances from Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) that no permits had been issued for construction waste exports to Malaysia.

The issue first came to light in August following reports that large quantities of construction and demolition waste had been transported into Pontian and dumped at several locations, including Kampung Sungai Karang, Kampung Sungai Senai and Kampung Simpang Kiri.

Investigations identified nine Malaysian companies allegedly linked to the transportation and dumping activities, prompting the Johor government to establish a special task force involving SWCorp, local authorities, police and the district administration.

On Aug 17, NEA informed SWCorp that Singapore would halt the export of construction and demolition waste to Malaysia. It reiterated that such waste was not permitted to be exported for disposal and reminded licensed waste management facilities to comply with regulations.

SWCorp said all construction waste must be disposed of at approved or gazetted facilities and warned that enforcement would be intensified to prevent further illegal dumping, in line with the Johor Clean City 2030 aspiration.
62b49bc7f7abf6f9: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.
This smell startup says its AI nose is as good as a human’s

In a New Jersey lab, researchers are trying to sniff every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with chemical analyses to train what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. Its goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”

Wiltschko claims the model has already achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence” and is helping fragrance brands design new scents. But Osmo has bigger ambitions, from detecting counterfeit goods to diagnosing diseases. Not everyone is convinced its technology can deliver.
How far could an AI-powered sense of smell really take us?
—Amit Katwala
Hydropower hit record lows in the US Southwest this summer
The US Southwest generated 28% less electricity via hydropower between April and August than the 10-year average, according to new data from the US Energy Information Administration.

Most hydropower plants in the US rely on dams to hold back water, creating reservoirs. But an extreme, prolonged drought has left water levels dangerously low in the region’s two largest reservoirs—and climate change is adding to the pressure.
Find out how climate change is threatening a vital source of renewable power.
—Casey Crownhart
MIT Technology Review Narrated: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom

Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of the US grid, helping move power efficiently across long distances. But they’re complicated and in short supply, and their basic design hasn’t changed much in about a century.

As electricity demand rises from EVs, data centers, and more, plans are emerging to modernize these grid staples. Solid-state versions could help ease supply concerns and cut power losses. The technology is still in development, but it could become a crucial part of our future grid.

What’s next for IVF

IVF has brought millions of babies into the world over the last four decades. But the process can still be slow, painful, and expensive—and far from guaranteed to work. Now, a wave of new technologies aims to change that.

Researchers are using AI to identify promising sperm and embryos, developing robotic systems that could automate parts of the IVF process, and even exploring controversial genetic editing techniques designed to prevent inherited disease.
The technologies could make IVF more effective and accessible. But they’re also raising difficult ethical questions about how far reproductive medicine should go.

9cb9694735c690ed: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia must not repeat its colonial-era experience with tin mining in developing its rare earth industry, Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) has warned.
He questioned the extent of the Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry's (Mosti) involvement in research and development (R&D) into rare earth processing.

"To this day, our country has rare earth supplies but no means, no approach and no technology to process them," he said while debating the ministry's allocation under the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat committee stage.

Radzi said growing interest from world powers in Malaysia's rare earth deposits was evident, noting that 80 per cent of the deposits were located in Terengganu, Kelantan, Perak, Kedah and Pahang, within forest reserves.
"Yesterday, the French president came to Malaysia, and one of his main aims was to discuss the supply of REE, or rare earths, from Malaysia," he said.
He also cited Malaysia's Agreement on Reciprocal Trade with the United States, saying rare earths were among its main components.

Radzi highlighted the government's decision to allow the export of up to 100 metric tonnes of raw rare earths for R&D, subject to a commitment to establish processing facilities in Malaysia within three years.
He questioned the extent of Mosti's involvement in developing domestic processing capabilities and whether it was collaborating with local universities.
He said he did not want private companies, particularly those with predominantly foreign shareholders, to reap most of the benefits from the country's mineral resources.
Drawing parallels with the tin industry, Radzi said Malaya produced about 55 per cent of the world's tin in 1900.

"The colonialists plundered the tin. They took the benefits of tin mining back to their own countries. Some of us benefited, but what did they leave behind? All that is left to us is the mining pools.
"In the end, what is left in our country, as the Bachok MP mentioned just now, is badly affected catchment areas, badly affected water supplies and very limited benefit to Malaysia," he said.

39fd3d79ccfcd86c: JERUSALEM: The body overseeing US President Donald Trump's plan to end the Gaza war accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their commitments to end hostilities, leaving the population of Gaza in dire conditions and the ceasefire in danger of collapse.

The 12-page Board of Peace report, seen by Reuters, is the body's second to the UN Security Council since the US-backed ceasefire came into effect 13 months ago. It offers a sobering assessment of progress made since then.
The board, established and headed by Trump, is expected to present the report's findings to a meeting of the council in New York at the end of November.

"The distance between what has been agreed and what is happening on the ground nonetheless remains the principal risk to the process," the report said, warning that "a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely."
Peace plan stalled

While the ceasefire has halted major fighting, the wider plan, which calls for Hamas to disarm, Israeli troops to withdraw and reconstruction to begin, has effectively stalled since soon after it came into effect last year.

Hamas agreed in July to a Board of Peace roadmap to surrender its weapons and transfer governance of Gaza to a civilian transitional authority, but Israel rejected the roadmap, saying it will not withdraw until Hamas is dismantled.
Israel has carried out near-daily strikes on Gaza, while the report said Hamas fighters have also continued attacks on Israeli troops.
"Every day that Israel continues strikes against Hamas targets, it delays putting Hamas' agreement to the roadmap to the test," the report said.
"Meanwhile, Hamas militant activity continues, the commitment to cease all military activities has not been met in full by the parties, and the population faces another winter in tents and rubble."

Senior Hamas official Basem Naim dismissed the report as "pure disinformation", accusing the Board of Peace of providing cover to Israel to evade its commitments under the plan to end the war and to continue its aggression in Gaza.
The office of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and a spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Israeli 'absence of decisions'

Gaza's population of more than 2 million Palestinians lives confined to around a third of the coastal territory, mostly in makeshift tents and damaged buildings, under the control of Hamas fighters. Israel occupies two-thirds of Gaza that has been largely razed and depopulated.

The report criticised Israel's government for an "absence of decisions" on arrangements to train and deploy a civilian Palestinian police force to replace Hamas as Gaza's law enforcement authority. It said this was impeding the full implementation of the plan.

It said restrictions imposed by Israel on supplies and equipment, alongside funding shortfalls, had hindered the ability of Gazans to prepare for and respond to seasonal flooding. Heavy rain inundated displacement camps last week across Gaza, and more rain is expected later this month.
Hamas, for its part, was collecting taxes on goods entering Gaza that were impacting the availability of basic commodities, the report said.
The Board of Peace was established by Trump to oversee his ambitious plan to end the war that Israel launched in response to Hamas-led attacks from Gaza in October 2023.

Around 1,200 people were killed in Israel in the 2023 Hamas attacks, while the Israeli assault on Gaza has since killed 74,000 Palestinians. More than 1,600 Palestinians, including many civilians, and five Israeli soldiers have been killed in Gaza since the US-mediated ceasefire was struck in October 2025.
Trump's plan received strong international backing, though the board itself has been met with scepticism from many of Washington's Western allies.

Netanyahu's right-wing coalition government remains in power in Israel in a caretaker capacity despite losing its majority in an inconclusive election last month. On Wednesday, defence minister Israel Katz said Israel would not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas was dismantled and Gaza was demilitarised.
9ca8c8ca2a0b5dbc: KUALA LUMPUR: Lac Med Bhd has secured a RM21.2 million contract to supply and integrate advanced angiography systems for cardiology and interventional radiology across three public hospitals in Malaysia.
The contract was awarded to its subsidiary, Lac Medical Supplies Sdn Bhd, by a local healthcare project partner.
The project involves the deployment and integration of advanced angiography systems at University Malaya Medical Centre, Hospital Melaka and Hospital Raja Permaisuri Bainun in Ipoh.
The latest contract follows another healthcare technology contract announced on Monday, bringing the group's order book to a record high of more than RM300 million.

Chief executive officer Liew Yoon Poh said surpassing RM300 million in its order book marked an important milestone for Lac Med and reflected the continued confidence healthcare providers had in the company's capabilities.
"These consecutive contract wins demonstrate the breadth of our integrated MedTech solutions across both public and private healthcare sectors.

"We remain focused on disciplined execution, strengthening our long-term customer relationships and building sustainable growth through a combination of project delivery and lifecycle services," Liew said in a statement.
The project is scheduled for handover by the fourth quarter of 2028.
be7c20779cdcc0d5: KUALA LUMPUR: Prosper Trading Sdn Bhd, together with its co-founders Tee Kim Tee @ Tee Ching Tee and Tee Cheng Hua, has acquired a collective 118.41 million shares, representing a 56.45 per cent stake in United Malacca Bhd, making its takeover offer for the plantation company unconditional.

In a statement, UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd, on behalf of the offerors, said the acceptance condition was met today after the offerers' aggregate shareholding in United Malacca exceeded the required 50 per cent threshold.

"Pursuant to subparagraph 12.01(3)(b) of the rules, the offeror and joint ultimate offerors shall keep the offer open for acceptances for at least 14 days from the unconditional date, which in any event, shall not be later than the 60th day from the posting date.

"Accordingly, we wish to inform that the closing time and date for the acceptance of the offer have been extended from 5 pm on Nov 23, 2026 to 5 pm on Dec 3, 2026, which is at least 14 days from the unconditional date.
428ac1da23812f5a: PETALING JAYA: Setiausaha Agung PKR Fuziah Salleh berkongsi surat memaparkan Timbalan Menteri Kerja Raya Ahmad Maslan memohon maaf kepada Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim atas 'kekhilafan kata-kata' baru-baru ini, yang mana pemimpin Umno itu didakwa menyindir Pakatan Harapan dengan 'pantun kencing'.

Menurut gambar yang dikongsi di Facebook itu, Ahmad memohon maaf atas kekhilafan kata-kata, termasuk pantun yang dilafazkan ketika sesi penggulungan perbahasan bagi Kementerian Kerja Raya di Dewan Rakyat pada 16 Nov lalu.
"Saya mengakui bahawa pemilihan kata tersebut tidak sesuai dengan tanggungjawab saya sebagai anggota pentadbiran dan kesal atas ketidakselesaan yang timbul," menurut surat bertarikh 17 Nov itu.
Ahmad menerangkan bahawa pantun kontroversi itu tidak terkandung dalam teks penggulungan perbahasan.
Menurutnya, pantun itu disampaikan ketika menjawab pertanyaan Ahli Parlimen mengenai pengurangan dan penghapusan tol.
"Saya bertanggungjawab sepenuhnya atas kata-kata tersebut dan perkataan 'kencing' dalam pantun berkenaan telah saya tarik balik di Parlimen," katanya.
Ahmad berkata beliau tidak berniat menjejaskan atau memutuskan hubungan kerjasama dalam kerajaan, dan mengulangi sokongan terhadap kerajaan dan kepimpinan Anwar sehingga akhir penggal pentadbiran.
"Sebagai anggota pentadbiran, saya akan terus melaksanakan amanah dengan profesional serta menjaga ketertiban bahasa dan semangat kerjasama ketika mewakili kerajaan," katanya.
Kelmarin, media melaporkan Dewan Rakyat kecoh apabila Ahmad menyelitkan pantun kontroversi itu ketika menjawab celahan Ahli Parlimen Beruas, Ngeh Koo Ham, berhubung isu penghapusan tol.
Susulan tindakan itu, beberapa Ahli Parlimen Pakatan Harapan mendesak Ahmad meletakkan jawatan sekiranya tidak lagi bersetuju dengan kerajaan sekarang.

Semalam, Ahmad memberitahu pemberita bahawa beliau tidak akan meletakkan jawatan susulan kontroversi 'pantun kencing', kerana beliau diberikan jawatan itu atas sokongan Umno dan Barisan Nasional, lapor Berita Harian.
"Terlajak perahu boleh diundur. Terlajak kata buruk padahnya," kata Fuziah dalam hantarannya, hari ini.
2f2671a6ef31a4fc: KUALA LUMPUR: Guan Chong Bhd's net profit surged more than sixfold to RM277.65 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM41.24 million a year earlier, driven by effective management of raw material purchases and cocoa ingredient sales positions.
The group said lower borrowings during the quarter also helped reduce finance costs.
Revenue, meanwhile, fell 38 per cent to RM2.31 billion from RM3.73 billion a year earlier, due to lower selling prices for cocoa products in line with declining cocoa bean prices.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, Guan Chong's net profit rose to RM654.25 million from RM184.04 million a year earlier, while revenue declined to RM6.73 billion from RM11.92 billion.
The group said chocolate demand was expected to improve over the next six months, supported by moderating cocoa prices and continued demand for premium chocolate.
"The premiumisation trend is expected to continue, while the longer-term demand outlook remains supported by growing preference for real chocolate products over compound alternatives.

"However, the potential impact of El Niño weather event in key cocoa-producing regions, together with structural supply challenges and geopolitical uncertainties, could continue to impact market sentiment and supply availability," it said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
While global cocoa supply has improved from the severe deficits seen previously, the company noted that market conditions remained susceptible to weather-related production disruptions.

Looking ahead, the group said it remained committed to its core cocoa ingredient processing business while expanding into the industrial chocolate segment and optimising production in line with changing market conditions.
57e792fde0e89924: HONG KONG: Screen legend Chow Yun Fat, 71, is showing no signs of slowing down as he gears up for a 20km challenge at Oxfam Trailwalker 2026 alongside members of his running club.
Held from Nov 20 to 22, the event primarily follows the MacLehose Trail and also retains its traditional 100km challenge.
According to reports, Chow recently hit the trails with fellow actor Raymond Wong to train for the run.
Having taken up hiking only at the age of 60, Chow modestly considers himself relatively inexperienced despite having explored much of the MacLehose Trail.
He also joked that a fear of snakes and ghosts was one reason he formed his own running club.
"I'm afraid of snakes and ghosts. If I run with them, at least they will get bitten before I do," he playfully told Hong Kong media.
Aside from personally recruiting new members—including Hong Kong actor Kent Cheng—Chow often arranges food for his group, saying the meals are the real highlight of their outings.
He recalled once bringing ingredients to cook claypot rice on the trail, ensuring everyone had a hearty meal after their run.
Wong, 51, said Chow often encourages the group to run a little further so they can explore more places and discover good food along the way.

While Wong believes having friends for company makes the experience more enjoyable, Chow acknowledged that running is no easy feat, noting that one must first endure the hardship before savouring the rewards.
Oxfam Trailwalker is an annual team endurance and fundraising event organised by the international charity Oxfam.
Participants form teams of four and work together to complete designated routes within 48 hours to raise funds for poverty alleviation and emergency relief efforts.
a88cea43abc39a34: KUALA KANGSAR: A Form Three student at a fully residential school here was found dead on the school grounds today.
Several police vehicles were seen entering the school compound this evening, believed to be in connection with investigations into the incident.
However, police have yet to issue an official statement or provide details surrounding the incident.

0eedfeb678c28116: PETALING JAYA: Deputy works minister Ahmad Maslan has apologised to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim over his choice of words in a pantun he recited in the Dewan Rakyat on Monday.
In a letter dated Nov 17 and received by the Prime Minister’s Office today, Ahmad acknowledged that the wording was inappropriate for a government officer.
He said the pantun was not part of his original winding-up speech, but was recited in response to a question from MPs on toll reductions and abolitions.
“Nevertheless, I take full responsibility for those words, and I have withdrawn the word 'kencing' in the pantun in Parliament,” he said in the letter.
“I had no intention of undermining or disrupting ties within the unity government led by the prime minister.
"My support for the government and the prime minister’s leadership remains until the end of the current administration’s term."
He said he would continue to discharge his responsibilities professionally, maintain decorum, and uphold the spirit of cooperation when representing the government.
On Monday, Ahmad had said toll abolition was a Pakatan Harapan pledge that Barisan Nasional had never made.
He then used a pantun to urge the public to support BN and Perikatan Nasional, warning against being "kena kencing" - a Malay expression for being cheated.
923ebe5486798a7b: BUDAPEST: Leaked Deutsche Bank documents reveal that a suspected Russian money-laundering network funnelled money through a Hungarian bank owned by allies of the country's ex-leader Viktor Orban, Hungarian media reported Wednesday.

International media, including The Financial Times, Le Monde and The New York Times, published reports Tuesday based on millions of leaked documents and emails that shine a light on questionable past practices at the German banking giant.
The media consortium found that several major companies involved were linked to the sanctioned Russian oligarch Oleg Deripaska.
The documents show that MKB, a bank partly owned by the Hungarian government, played a key role in a suspected Russian "laundromat" network, the investigative site Direkt36 said.

MKB came under the control of businessmen closely tied to Orban, the Kremlin-friendly prime minister at the time, in 2017 and later helped finance his far-right allies abroad, including France's Marine Le Pen.
The Russian network transferred at least €1.7 billion (US$1.9 million) between 2017 and 2020 and displayed "numerous signs of organised crime", according to Direkt36.
"MKB Bank played a key role in the network's operation, having initiated and received the highest proportion of transfers," Direkt36 said.
Five of the network's 15 key companies, which were mostly registered in Hong Kong and Cyprus, held accounts at the bank despite having no apparent connection to Hungary, it added.
"These had received and sent at least €460 million," the report said.

Although MKB claimed it had closed most of its offshore client accounts in 2019, Deutsche Bank did not see a "significant" decrease in "the high proportion of transactions originating from non-resident clients", according to the article.

This led the German banking giant to sever its longstanding relationship with the Hungarian bank, which caused a brief "panic" at MKB until it secured a replacement arrangement with the Dutch bank ING, Direkt36 said.
MKB and its successor MBH Bank have come under media scrutiny in Hungary for financing projects linked to Orban's allies.

Austrian media on Wednesday also reported that documents from the Deutsche Bank leak showed payments from a suspected money-laundering network to several Austrian companies, including the private jet operator Avcon Jet and helicopter services provider Wucher.
One of the network's Hong Kong-registered companies, Dempshire Corporation, had ties to Deripaska and channelled more than €130 million over three years, Der Standard reported.
a73424645a5daf48: Fifteen people have been arrested over an alleged scam that squeezed more money from investment fraud victims by offering to help recover their losses.

City of London Police searched 17 London addresses on November 11 and apprehended 14 men and one woman. All have since been released on bail. Investigators say the suspected fraudsters posed as regulators to persuade previous victims that compensation was available.
Reports submitted through the UK's Report Fraud service helped investigators trace the compensation pitch to around 3,000 recipients since October 2025.
Most victims were elderly, police said. The offers arrived by letter and email, promising redress for earlier investment losses.

City of London Police said the victims were initially targeted by a range of investment scams related to art, carbon credits, land, whisky, wine, and pensions, and that some took place more than a decade prior to their re-victimization.
Targets were directed to a company that demanded a holding fee before supposedly reclaiming their money. Police say those who paid were left further out of pocket.

"Today's action sends a clear message to those who target vulnerable people for financial gain: you will be pursued and will face robust action," said Nik Adams, deputy commissioner at the City of London Police.
"Behind every fraud report is a real person whose trust has been damaged, and in some cases, whose life savings have been stolen. We know the impact of these crimes can be devastating.

"This case highlights the importance of reporting fraud through the Report Fraud service. Information provided by victims helped investigators link reports together, uncover the wider conspiracy, and identify those involved. It is a powerful reminder that every report counts and can play a vital role in bringing offenders to justice."
The investigation also extends beyond London, with police identifying locations linked to the case in Kent and Hertfordshire.
The searches resulted in officers seizing cash, drugs, and other high-value items, including a watch worth around £230,000, with the total haul valued at more than £2 million.
Police put losses identified so far at £1.5 million and expect that figure to rise as the investigation continues.
Knowing the details of an earlier scam doesn't make a caller trustworthy, police warned. That information can be used to sell victims a second fraud.
Report Fraud has also highlighted substantial losses in other scams affecting older people.

Fraudsters exploiting positions of trust stole a reported £93.8 million during 2025/26. People aged 70 and over lost more than £51 million, with relatives, friends, carers, and others entrusted with their finances among the perpetrators. Report Fraud received 3,812 reports in this category.
"The impact of fraud extends far beyond financial loss, especially when it is carried out by those who are trusted by the victim," said Mark Evans, president at the Law Society of England and Wales.

Similarly, at the end of October, Report Fraud said £24.3 million was stolen between January and August 2026 through AI-augmented investment scams, with people aged 60 and over accounting for nearly 80 percent of reports.
However, it's not always the elderly in scammers' crosshairs. Those in the 30-39 age bracket accounted for the most reports in one of the most lucrative frauds affecting Brits in recent times.

Payment diversion fraud, which tricks victims into paying a criminal's bank account instead of the intended recipient's, resulted in £101 million in losses in the 2025/26 financial year, according to Report Fraud's figures. ®

519003cafbe0570f: KOTA BARU: A policeman was killed after the motorcycle he was riding collided with a car at Pulau Melaka here today.
Corporal Muhamad Alimi Kamarudin, 35, died at the scene in the 5.15pm collision after sustaining serious head and body injuries.
He was attached to the weapons division at the Kota Baru district police station.
Kota Baru district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Azmir Damiri confirmed the incident, saying police would issue a statement soon.
Meanwhile, the victim's sister, Siti Nuradila Kamarudin, said the family was informed of the accident at about 5.30pm.
"His wife, Khalidah Adilah Zainuddin, told me she had called him about an hour before the accident.
"He told her he was on his way home to Ketereh after completing his duties," she said.
The 38-year-old personal tutor was speaking when met at the Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia (HUSM) forensic unit tonight.
Alimi, the third of five siblings, was the eldest son in the family. He leaves behind his wife and two children, aged four and seven.
8d4416ac37f1e0b7: KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Industries Bhd posted a higher net profit of RM163.67 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 2027) compared with RM154.90 million in the same period last year.

Revenue rose to RM997.18 million in 1Q 2027 from RM983.38 million previously, primarily attributed to a better sales mix of motorcycle models and lower raw material costs resulting from favourable foreign exchange movements.
Hong Leong Industries declared an interim single-tier dividend of 35 sen per share for the quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, to be paid on Dec 16, 2026.
On the outlook, the company said demand for motorcycles is expected to remain stable amid a more competitive market with the influx of Chinese motorcycles.
"The group will continue to strengthen its product offerings and brand positioning, optimise its product mix, enhance after-sales service, and maintain disciplined cost management," it said.
52d22fd553083837: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission has denied agreeing to reward a foreign businessman in exchange for information to help recover assets linked to the 1MDB scandal.

MACC said the document outlining the proposed rewards and sharing of proceeds from asset recovery was merely a draft submitted by French-Syrian businessman Bachar Kiwan and had never been agreed to or signed by the commission.

The clarification follows allegations by Sarawak Report concerning MACC’s dealings with Kiwan, who claimed to possess information that could help Malaysia recover billions of ringgit linked to the 1MDB scandal.

In a statement, MACC said it conducted an internal investigation into the allegations to determine whether further action was necessary, and meetings between its officers and Kiwan were part of normal investigative procedures to examine and verify information he had provided in connection with efforts to recover 1MDB assets.
Representatives from the Attorney-General's Chambers attended every discussion, it said, adding that the meetings did not mean the commission recognised any of Kiwan's claims or status.

"Regarding allegations about rewards and the sharing of proceeds from asset recovery, MACC wishes to stress that the document in question was a draft of proposed terms submitted by the businessman and was never agreed to or signed by the commission," it said.
It said it had decided not to continue cooperating with Kiwan after obtaining official documents and authenticated records through a mutual legal assistance request to the Kuwaiti authorities.
As a result, it said, the information offered by the businessman was no longer a primary requirement for its investigation.
MACC also clarified that Kiwan was not recognised as a protected person under the Whistleblower Protection Act 2010, and that this had been communicated to him during a meeting on Dec 2 last year.
Sarawak Report had said that Kiwan had approached Malaysian authorities with information he claimed could help trace funds allegedly laundered through Kuwait as part of the 1MDB scandal.

According to the publication, Kiwan claimed that he could trace up to 160 million Kuwaiti dinars (about RM2.11 billion) through the network of assets linked to Sheikh Sabah Jaber Mubarak Al-Sabah, the son of a former Kuwaiti prime minister.
It said Kuwait had notified Malaysia of its readiness to return 15 million Kuwaiti dinars (about RM200 million) from funds linked to Sheikh Sabah.

The report said the proposed terms of engagement, dated April 26, 2026, outlined a success-based fee arrangement under which an alleged local law firm representing Kiwan would receive 45% of any whistleblower reward, Kiwan another 45%, and his Paris-based law firm the remaining 10%.
The report said the document appeared to have been signed by a lawyer but was never signed by Kiwan or his legal advisers, who were concerned about the arrangement.
MACC officers were alleged to have recommended a member of former prime minister Najib Razak's legal team to represent Kiwan, a claim which the commission denied.
“MACC was never involved (in appointing lawyers) as the matter fell outside its jurisdiction,” it said.
“The right to appoint a lawyer rests solely with the individual concerned, and the withdrawal of the law firm involved was also the firm’s own decision.”
48c3827e858de6ee: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.

Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter's moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a "commemorative phonograph record," in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.

About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs' overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.
bae9e4bebba85d6d: KUALA LUMPUR: A man died when a tree fell and crushed the motorcycle he was riding at Jalan Set 2/8, Setia Eco Templer, Selayang, this afternoon.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Ashbar said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 2.19pm.
He said six personnel and two fire engines from the Selayang Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the scene.
"Upon arrival at 2.28pm, the operations commander reported that a tree had fallen and crushed an Isuzu lorry and a Yamaha NMAX motorcycle.
"A male motorcyclist was trapped and unconscious. Firefighters then proceeded to extricate the victim," he said in a statement.
Ashrul Riezal said the victim was pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from the Health Ministry.
5e0c8a17cf076891: KUALA LUMPUR: The bidding process for the takeover of Boustead Plantations Bhd is not based solely on the size of the bidder but also takes into account other criteria, the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) said.
These include the bidder's incorporation status, ability to complete the transaction, strategic suitability and long-term commitment to stakeholders.

LTAT, which controls Boustead Plantations, said its key investment activities were carried out through a competitive bidding process guided by pre-established evaluation criteria, with an emphasis on integrity and good governance.
The fund said bidders must be either government-linked companies (GLCs) or Bumiputera-owned companies, or both, with their status verified by an independent third-party adviser.

"Certainty of execution encompasses proven financing capabilities, while strategic suitability is assessed based on each bidder's capabilities and commitments, rather than solely on the size of the bidder.
"Continuity of existing commitments to the Armed Forces community is also taken into consideration," it said in a statement.
It was reported on Tuesday that LTAT had chosen Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd to take over Boustead Plantations at an estimated price of RM4.3 billion.
Sources told Berita Harian that Achi Jaya was understood to have beaten SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd, two companies with larger plantation operations, in the bidding process.

On the reported proposed transaction, LTAT confirmed that all bidders were either GLCs or Bumiputera-owned companies, or both, in accordance with the guidelines of the Companies Commission of Malaysia.

"The transaction and the evaluation of the bids submitted have been carried out through a stringent process to safeguard LTAT's governance standards and credibility, taking into account the established criteria.

"As the transaction remains subject to ongoing processes and no definitive agreement has been signed, LTAT will make the appropriate announcements and disclosures at the appropriate time, in accordance with the relevant requirements," it said.
c8e47a9b5009f0cc: KUALA LUMPUR: JS Solar Holding Bhd's unit JS Solar Sdn Bhd has secured a RM30 million contract from NUR Power Ventures Sdn Bhd for a rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) and battery energy storage system (Bess) project.
Under the contract, JS Solar will undertake the engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning works for the project, which is targeted to begin commercial operations by July 1, 2027.
JS Solar Holding said the contract marked further progress in its collaboration with NUR Power Sdn Bhd, the holding company of NUR Power Ventures.
The two companies signed a memorandum of understanding in February to explore strategic collaboration in rooftop solar renewable energy projects.
JS Solar Holding managing director Johnson Chai Jeun Sian said the latest contract would strengthen the company's capabilities in integrated renewable energy solutions.

"The integration of rooftop solar PV and BESS reflects the evolving requirements of renewable energy projects, and this award provides JS Solar with another opportunity to further build our capabilities across both technologies," he said.

"With a targeted commercial operation date of 1 July 2027, our immediate priority will be to ensure disciplined project execution and work closely with NUR Power towards the successful delivery of the project.

"We remain focused on pursuing suitable opportunities that leverage our experience in solar PV while progressively expanding our capabilities in complementary energy solutions such as Bess," he added.
JS Solar Holding said the project would further expand its involvement in Bess, complementing its existing solar PV engineering, contracting and operations and maintenance services.
The ACE Market-listed company provides solar PV solutions for residential, commercial, industrial and utility-scale projects, including rooftop, ground-mounted and floating installations.
a65f3c7501f44533: KUALA LUMPUR: National bowler Shaqeem Izwan Teh is determined to win the Boys Open title in his final attempt when the Milo Storm U22 International Junior All-Stars return to Sunway Mega Lanes next month.
The 22-year-old, runner-up to South Korea's Kim Soo Han last year, has competed in the annual tournament since he was seven without claiming its flagship crown.
Shaqeem, a former Under-12 champion, said the pressure affected him in last year's final and he hopes to handle the occasion better this time.
"I feel a bit pressured because it's my last year, and I've never won the Boys Open title," he said.
"Last year, I couldn't handle the pressure at Sunway. I really hope I can play better and handle it this time.
"I've targeted this title since I was 16. Last year, I was almost there, so I hope I can finally do it."
The RM30,000 champion's cheque is not his main motivation.
"I just want to win the title. I don't care about the prize money."
National bowler Adania Mohd Redzwan also returns to the tournament after losing the 2024 Girls Open final to Singapore's Hazel Tan.
Adania, 21, missed last year's edition because of SEA Games commitments and is aiming for a podium finish rather than setting a title-or-bust target.
"My aim is to finish in the top three," said Adania, who won two gold medals at the World Youth Championships in Kuching in July.
"Every tournament is different. Even though we train here every day, it depends on the conditions and who we play against.
"It's going to be tough, but I'll try to adapt."
The Girls Open field includes defending champion Lavinia Kho, 2023 winner Adelia Nur Irwan Syazalee and Hazali, while Soo Han will defend the Boys Open crown.
The Dec 1-13 event has drawn more than 900 entries from 16 countries, with Singapore sending the largest overseas contingent at 280 bowlers.
Hong Kong's reigning World Cup champion Jovi Ma is also competing.
Organised by Sunway Mega Lanes, the tournament offers RM265,800 in prize money, making it Asia's richest junior bowling event.

The Super Junior category, now in its second year for bowlers aged 29 and below, will feature former world champion Rafiq Ismail, who won the Boys Open in 2012, and newly crowned Asian champion Gillian Lim.
6a1bb86410181c50: PETALING JAYA: Harga minyak tanpa subsidi akan turun secara menyeluruh bermula esok, bagi minggu kedua berturut-turut.
Menurut Kementerian Kewangan, harga RON95 dan diesel tanpa subsidi masing-masing akan turun 15 sen, menjadikan harga runcitnya RM3.72 seliter dan RM4.72 seliter, sehingga 25 Nov.
RON97 pula akan dijual pada harga RM4 seliter, iaitu turun 20 sen.
RON95 di bawah skim BUDI95 akan terus dijual pada harga RM1.99 seliter, manakala diesel kekal pada RM2.10 seliter di bawah inisiatif BUDI Diesel.

Petrol bersubsidi di bawah Sistem Kawalan Petrol Bersubsidi (SKPS) akan kekal pada RM2.05 seliter, manakala diesel bersubsidi di bawah Sistem Kawalan Diesel Bersubsidi (SKDS) akan dijual pada harga RM2.15 seliter.
Dalam kenyataan, kementerian itu berkata, kerajaan persekutuan akan terus melindungi orang ramai dan perniagaan daripada kesan ketidaktentuan global melalui subsidi.
"Peruntukan hampir RM40 bilion disediakan untuk subsidi bahan api pada tahun hadapan bagi membantu rakyat mengurangkan tekanan kos sara hidup," katanya.
bf94fa3d5e646117: BRUSSELS: The European Commission on Wednesday proposed a new €45 billion (US$49.5 billion) loan to Ukraine to help fill a funding gap of €70 billion for next year as Kyiv continues its fight against Russia's 2022 invasion.
European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen said Ukraine would only need to repay the loan after Russia had paid reparations for damage caused by the war.

The planned measure, which requires approval from EU member countries, would come on top of a similar loan of €90 billion to Ukraine agreed by EU leaders at the end of last year to fund Ukraine in 2026 and 2027.
"Five years since the start of this war of aggression, Europe stands united," von der Leyen told reporters in Brussels. "We are as committed as ever to support Ukraine in war and in peace."
Kyiv's other international partners would be expected to provide the rest of the money to fill next year's funding gap, von der Leyen said.
The Commission, the executive body of the 27-nation European Union, proposed that up to €25 billion from the new loan could be spent on military aid and up to €20 billion on general budget support.
To finance the loan, the European Commission would borrow on behalf of the EU on international markets, officials said.
Intensified Russian attacks mean Ukraine needs more cash

European economy commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said Ukraine needed additional support because Russia is intensifying attacks on critical infrastructure and disrupting trade, particularly by blocking Black Sea export routes.

"For almost five years, Ukraine has stood guard against the Russian aggression that also threatens our citizens, our territory, and our way of life. Our support gives Ukraine a crucial strategic partner," he said.
