53bf28c36494803d: The activist admits his mental state has been negatively affected by the 10-year sentence increase
Originally published on Global Voices
Joshua Wong released from Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre on June 17, 2019. HKFP's File photo.

This article was originally published by Hong Kong Free Press on November 16, 2026. The following version is edited and republished on Global Voices under a content partnership agreement. It is also part of Global Voices’ November 2026 Spotlight series, “Justice as infrastructure.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

In a letter from a Hong Kong prison earlier this year, jailed activist Joshua Wong expressed dread over the looming sentence in his foreign collusion case. “Fretting about whether it’s 2032 or 2037, my mental state is hardly all right,” he wrote in Chinese, weighing when he might regain his freedom.
The agony inevitably stems from this: What if it’s 2037? Well, it’s easy [for people] to sympathise in the moment, but it’s difficult to be consistent, and it will only get harder.

The 30-year-old pro-democracy activist has already spent almost six years behind bars over various offences and was set for release in January 2026, until authorities charged him last year with conspiring to collude with foreign forces — the second case against him under the Beijing-imposed national security law. His case is one of the most high-profile examples of changing judicial norms in Hong Kong.
A prison letter Joshua Wong wrote to friend and former fellow student activist Louis Lee in February 2026. This photo was taken on September 30, 2026. Photo by Kyle Lam/HKFP. Used with permission.

On November 5, just two months before he was due to be released, a court sentenced him to 10 more years in prison for colluding with foreign forces. He is now expected to serve until late 2036, when he turns 40.

Standing in the courtroom as his new sentence was announced, Wong shook his head slightly and made notes, but appeared calm. Judge William Tam ruled that Wong’s offence was one of a “grave nature” under the national security law, which carries a minimum penalty of 10 years in jail and up to life imprisonment.
The judge knocked off three years from a 13-year starting sentence for Wong’s guilty plea.

In prison correspondence shared with HKFP by two close friends ahead of Wong’s sentencing, the former poster child of Hong Kong’s democracy movement had at times reflected on the weight of facing an additional decade behind bars. He expressed anxiety over fading from the memory of his friends — and from society at large. In one letter, Wong wrote:
I have no idea how much more I will lose in the passing of time. Responsibility is, in fact, response-ability. But who will respond? I can’t help but ponder and doubt.

Once a pro-democracy activist dedicated first and foremost to Hong Kong’s political future, Wong began campaigning as a charismatic, eloquent student leader who dared to stand up to the authorities — even to Beijing. Hong Kong is an overseas territory of China, and has increasingly been pressured to conform to China’s political goals in recent years, despite agreements that Hong Kong would retain “a high degree of autonomy” when handed over to China in 1997. A Netflix documentary about him is succinctly titled “Joshua: Teenager vs. Superpower.”

Yet, after years behind bars, Wong has changed. The teenager who focused single-mindedly on Hong Kong’s democracy movement has become even more caring for those around him despite being separated by prison walls, according to his friends.
Tiffany Chin, a former student activist who campaigned alongside Wong, said. The pair were once romantically involved and are now friends. She shared:
For me, it doesn’t feel like we’re the only ones supporting him. In fact, he has been supporting people on the outside in his own way.
And, with the political causes he once championed now firmly crushed, Wong has turned inward to reflect on himself. In another letter, he wrote:
We had held such high aspirations for society from a young age, we should hold ourselves to the same standard. Only by refusing a life of mediocrity can we be worthy of the world we envisioned.
From “robot” to caring friend

On a bright summer day in June 2025, while serving a sentence for subversion at Stanley Prison, Wong was arrested behind bars and brought to court the same day on a fresh charge of conspiracy to collude with foreign forces.
The prosecution came without warning. That day, Chin and Louis Lee, another longtime friend of Wong’s, rushed to the court after hearing the news, but failed to see him in person.

Authorities accused him of conspiring with Nathan Law — another high-profile, pro-democracy student activist — in 2020 to collude with foreign elements, citing Wong’s sharing of Law’s social media posts calling for international sanctions against Hong Kong as evidence.
The unexpected new charge was devastating to Wong. That month, he confessed he was under a lot of pressure — a vulnerability he rarely showed in the past, Chin said.

After so many prison terms and all the ups and downs over the last decade… he seldom openly showed vulnerability. So when he felt the need to say so bluntly that he was not OK, I truly believed he wasn’t.

Having begun campaigning at the age of 14, Wong has been in and out of prison throughout his years of activism. He now has a total of eight criminal convictions, including three separate offences linked to unlawful assembly and two national security offences.
Joshua Wong is photographed inside the Lai Chi Kwok Reception Centre on March 4, 2021. Photo via HKFP. Used with permission.

Born in 1996 to a Christian family – one year before Hong Kong was handed over to China from British rule – Wong rose to prominence in 2011 when he co-founded student protest group Scholarism amid a public outcry against a proposed patriotic education curriculum.

The following year, Scholarism activists occupied the forecourt outside Hong Kong government headquarters and staged a hunger strike to protest what they described as a “brainwashing” curriculum. In a widely reported encounter, the teenager Wong twice refused to shake hands with then-city leader Leung Chun-ying, who visited the protest site alongside education officials.
Hundreds of thousands of people rallied behind Wong and his fellow student activists, forcing the government to back down and shelve the proposal.

But the teenage campaigner was also viewed as somewhat distant and domineering among the inner circle of Scholarism. Lee, who mainly handled protest logistics at that time, described his relationship with Wong as “almost like that of a boss and subordinate.”

Chin, who joined Scholarism around 2013, similarly described Wong as a deeply rational figure who seldom expressed his emotions. “Ten years ago, everyone described him as someone without many feelings,” she said. “Like a robot.”
Wong might even come across as “rude,” she added, noting that he rarely said thanks to others during that period.

A large part of Wong’s youth coincided with a period of escalating social movements in Hong Kong. Just two years after the anti-patriotic education protests, the city saw the 79-day Umbrella Movement in 2014. Wong, then aged 17, took centre stage in mobilising public support for student protesters, who demanded democratic reform and universal suffrage.

In a demonstration that sparked the Umbrella Movement, Wong and other student leaders led protesters into the forecourt of the government headquarters in an action dubbed “Reclaiming Civic Square,” seeking to escalate their campaign. That eventually resulted in Wong’s first criminal conviction.

In 2016, Wong and fellow student leaders Alex Chow and Nathan Law were found guilty of unlawful assembly. Though initially spared prison, Wong later served around 69 days behind bars – his first jail term – following a government appeal in 2017. His penalty was ultimately quashed by the Court of Final Appeal in 2018.

Scholarism disbanded in 2016. Wong and several former members, as well as young activists like Law, went on to establish Demosisto, a political party advocating for “democratic self-determination” in the city. Wong served as general secretary.
Lee and Chin did not join the new party, and they grew estranged from Wong during that period.

That year, Law was elected to the Legislative Council, making him the youngest lawmaker in Hong Kong history at the age of 23. He won over 50,000 votes, giving Demosisto a strong popular mandate. The prospect of youth democracy activism appeared bright at the time, but Law was eventually disqualified from his seat in 2017 following an oath-taking controversy.
From left: Joshua Wong, Agnes Chow, and Nathan Law, photographed on March 10, 2018. Photo via HKFP. Used with permission.
Reconnections
It was only after Wong’s detention in late 2020 that Lee and Chin reconnected with him, beginning with an exchange of letters.

In 2019, citywide protests and unrest triggered by a controversial extradition bill engulfed the city. Wong and Demosisto were heavily involved in the protests, with the activist frequently lobbying foreign governments to impose sanctions on Hong Kong officials and halt the export of crowd control equipment to the city’s police force.

Then, in June 2020, Beijing imposed the national security law, effectively crushing political dissent in the city. Demosisto disbanded on the eve of the law’s enactment, while Nathan Law left Hong Kong in self-exile.
Written by Hong Kong Free Press
c722a5b1c9188d1c: SHENZHEN: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin.

Thursday's trilateral has triggered fears that the three powerful men could make decisions on the fate of Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv and Europe and seek to carve up the world into 21st-century spheres of influence.
Washington had signalled that Ukraine – something Xi vehemently sees as not China's problem – was not expected to be addressed before Trump said that it would.
Xi welcomed Trump upon his landing at Shenzhen's Bao'an International Airport, AFP footage showed, returning the gesture of the US president's greeting at Joint Base Andrews in September.

"I look forward to an in-depth exchange of views with you on major issues concerning China-US relations, Asia-Pacific cooperation, and the global landscape, with the aim of advancing a constructive, strategically stable relationship between our two nations," Xi told Trump, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.
'Warm welcome'
China is hosting the annual meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec), a regional forum of 21 economies around the Pacific rim.
Trump descended the stairs from his plane to be met by Xi, as well as renditions of both countries' national anthems and fighter jets that flew overhead and left colourful vapour trails.
The pair strolled down a red carpet lined with people waving pom-poms, brandishing Chinese and American national flags, and shouting: "A warm welcome to you!"
A motorcade of dark limousines later carried Trump into the city, where the streets had been cleared of traffic, an AFP reporter observed.

Security is tight ahead of Thursday's trilateral meeting that is expected to include discussions of the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, according to Washington, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February.
Beijing has long maintained that the US and Russia should reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile.
Sanctions 'failed': Putin
Earlier on Wednesday, Putin struck a defiant tone on his war in Ukraine, saying Western sanctions provoked by the 2022 invasion had "failed".
Addressing the Apec gathering, the Russian leader said he expected the trilateral summit to be "highly useful".
"At a time when military-political risks are on the rise, what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums," Putin said.
The Russian leader has been largely shunned by the West since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine but has found an audience with Trump.
However, "full-scale" talks solely between Putin and Trump are unlikely to take place during their visits to China, Moscow said, according to Russian state media.
Canadian prime minister Mark Carney, also in Shenzhen, said sanctions would "continue to increase as long as this war goes on".
Putin and Xi's meeting was already their fifth this year, including one by video link. The two men have long touted their strong personal friendship.
Xi urged yet closer ties with Moscow, saying the nations should "leverage the mechanisms for exchanges between the two countries' governments, legislative bodies, militaries and political parties".
The Chinese and Russian leaders were expected to talk about energy and finance, and then – in a smaller format – foreign policy, including Ukraine and North Korea, Russian officials said.
Kim incoming?
Trump's visit to China comes after a trip to the Philippines, where a day earlier he met fellow leaders of the Quad – Australia, Japan and India – for the first time in his second term.
The grouping is broadly aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence.
He said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and Kim Jong Un at his next stop in Shenzhen, saying the North Korean leader "would like" to meet in China.
US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Wednesday stopped short of confirming the meeting with Kim.
"If we have a problem with North Korea, the only way we're ever going to solve it is if we engage with them," Rubio said in Manila.
Trump was in the Philippines for a summit of the 11-member Asean, where there were protests against a US supply chain initiative.
The spectre of Trump's ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large over his recent travels.
Chinese premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a "countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism" while touting Beijing's own expanding trade with Asean.
On Tuesday, a combative Trump doubled down, saying the United States would catch China in rare-earths production "within 10 months".
d1c0f3f0d45e2a5b: United Launch Alliance (ULA) says poor booster performance appears to have doomed Sunday's Vulcan mission, which lost an Amazon Leo satellite payload on the rocket's return to flight.

ULA's initial assessment points to trouble almost immediately. "Early indications are that just after liftoff the launch vehicle experienced low booster performance," it said. As a result, stage separation occurred at too low an altitude, and the rocket was not traveling fast enough for the payload to reach orbit.

The second stage appeared to perform well, with its RL10 engines operating as planned, but that wasn't enough to make up for the shortfall, and the mission failed. ULA lost telemetry approximately ten minutes into flight.

An investigation is underway, led by ULA and overseen by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which had to activate two Debris Response Areas where debris was falling. The agency directs aircraft to leave these areas, and others are prevented from entering.

Previous flights had been blighted by problems with the solid rocket boosters, designed to give the rocket a kick at launch. Those issues prompted a stand-down while investigators examined the cause. This time, ULA said: "All indications are that the solid rocket booster performance was nominal, following nozzle improvements implemented for this launch."

Attention therefore turns to Vulcan's liquid-fueled core stage, powered by two Blue Origin BE-4 engines, though that does not establish an engine fault. Fuel delivery or another first-stage system could also be responsible, and the investigation is ongoing.

The BE-4 also powers Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket, which exploded on the launchpad during a ground test in May. In August, Blue Origin boss Dave Limp said that the issue originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the BE-4 engines. Modifications were made to deal with the problem.

The upper stage's apparently normal performance may offer some reassurance to NASA, although the investigation remains at an early stage. The agency dropped the delayed Exploration Upper Stage earlier this year and is pursuing a stretched Centaur V alongside its existing interim cryogenic propulsion stage as options for Artemis IV.
NASA is targeting Artemis IV for early 2028 and Artemis V for later that year.
ULA said: "We truly understand the impact this has on our customers and are committed to returning to flight as safely and quickly as we can."

The failure also dents ULA's otherwise impressive launch record. A predecessor of Vulcan, the Atlas V, has a 100 percent success record for payloads reaching orbit. However, it uses Russian RD-180 engines, a dependency the US wishes to remove. ®
851b85ea40123810: SHENZHEN: Malaysia sedang mendapatkan penjelasan lanjut daripada Amerika Syarikat (AS) berhubung sekatan baharu ke atas eksport cip kecerdasan buatan (AI), khususnya mengenai keperluan pelesenan serta penyediaan perkhidmatan pusat data kepada pihak ketiga.

Menteri Pelaburan, Perdagangan dan Industri Johari Abdul Ghani berkata, Malaysia telah berhubung dengan pihak berkuasa AS termasuk Kedutaan AS dan wakil perdagangannya bagi mendapatkan perincian rasmi mengenai peraturan tersebut serta implikasinya terhadap pengendali pusat data.

Johari berkata, Malaysia akan memaklumkan kepada pemegang kepentingan kesemua 117 projek pusat data yang telah diluluskan untuk memastikan pematuhan sebaik sahaja Washington memaklumkan secara rasmi mengenai keperluan tersebut.
Sebahagian daripada pusat data itu sudahpun beroperasi, manakala yang lain sedang dalam pembinaan.

Beliau berkata, pengendali yang ingin mendapatkan unit pemprosesan grafik (GPU) keluaran AS untuk pusat data mereka perlu mematuhi peraturan AS, termasuk keperluan pelesenan serta prosedur usaha wajar yang dikenakan terhadap pembeli.

“Jika anda mahukan cip GPU dari AS untuk pusat data anda, anda perlu mematuhi peraturan AS. Sesiapa yang bersedia untuk mematuhinya, patuhi (peraturan itu), kemudian barulah anda boleh membeli cip tersebut,” katanya kepada wartawan Malaysia di luar acara Mesyuarat Pemimpin Ekonomi Apec hari ini.

Johari berkata, bagi pembeli yang pelanggannya terdiri daripada syarikat atau penyedia perkhidmatan berskala besar AS, keperluan pelesenan mereka boleh disahkan, manakala urus niaga yang melibatkan pelanggan dari negara lain mungkin memerlukan penelitian menyeluruh serta pemeriksaan 'kenali pelanggan anda' (KYC) oleh pihak berkuasa AS.

Katanya, Malaysia tidak mengeluarkan cip tersebut, sebaliknya menyediakan kemudahan bagi operasi pusat data, justeru, pengendali yang menggunakan GPU dari AS perlu mematuhi peraturan yang mengawal selia teknologi berkenaan.
Mengenai dakwaan Malaysia dijadikan sebagai hab pemindahan bagi cip AI yang dikenakan sekatan eksport itu, Johari berkata, kerajaan sedang menjalankan siasatan.
Beliau menegaskan kerajaan masih belum menerima sebarang bukti dokumen rasmi yang menunjukkan penyewa pusat data telah memperdagangkan atau mengeksport semula cip tersebut.

Katanya, siasatan akan merangkumi semakan dengan pihak Kastam bagi menentukan sama ada terdapat sebarang GPU yang dieksport semula, termasuk mengenal pasti pihak yang terlibat serta meneliti senarai muatan penghantaran dan pengisytiharan yang berkaitan.
“Saya masih belum melihat dokumen yang menunjukkan bahawa sesetengah pemain ini, iaitu penyewa yang mengendalikan pusat data tersebut, memperdagangkan cip itu," katanya.

“Jika mereka melakukan eksport semula, kami ingin tahu siapa pihak tersebut, dan mereka perlu mengemukakan senarai muatan yang telah mereka serahkan. Hanya selepas itu barulah kami boleh ambil tindakan lanjut. Kami tidak boleh sewenang-wenangnya membuat tuduhan."

Beliau berkata, AS sebagai pengeluar cip tersebut, harus menjalankan siasatan rapi terhadap pembeli dan memaklumkan kepada Malaysia mengenai syarikat yang berhasrat membawa masuk GPU ke dalam negara bagi tujuan operasi pusat data, sekali gus membolehkan pihak berkuasa memantau penggunaannya.

Tambahnya, Malaysia komited untuk memastikan perniagaan yang beroperasi di negara ini mematuhi peraturan dan undang-undang termasuk yang dikenakan oleh negara lain bagi melindungi harta intelek dan teknologi strategik.
Malaysia mengalu-alukan pelaburan pusat data, namun pengendali perlu mematuhi peraturan yang mengawal selia cip jika mereka ingin terus beroperasi di negara ini, katanya.

Sekatan baharu AS itu, katanya, tidak semestinya menjejaskan daya tarikan Malaysia sebagai destinasi pelaburan, namun boleh membawa implikasi kepada pengendali yang gagal mematuhi peraturan tersebut, terutamanya dalam mendapatkan pelanggan.

Johari berkata, Malaysia juga sedang mendapatkan penjelasan mengenai sekatan terkini yang merangkumi penyediaan perkhidmatan pusat data, memandangkan peraturan tersebut menjangkaui aspek eksport semula fizikal GPU, malah turut merangkumi penggunaan kapasiti pengkomputeran bagi pihak ketiga.

Beliau berkata, Malaysia masih belum menerima garis panduan rasmi mengenai perkara itu dan terus berhubung dengan pihak berkuasa AS bagi memahami skop sekatan tersebut serta bagaimana pematuhannya akan dipantau.

Pentadbiran Donald Trump pada Isnin mengeluarkan peraturan yang menetapkan sekatan baharu ke atas eksport cip ke pusat data di luar negara, yang membolehkan syarikat China memperoleh akses kepada cip AI berteknologi tinggi untuk melatih model AI mereka.

Peraturan itu juga mewajibkan syarikat di Singapura, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia dan Brazil untuk memohon lesen eksport AS bagi cip teknologi paling canggih, bertujuan untuk mengurangkan risiko cip tersebut dialihkan secara haram.
1510a3bae297b37d: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today increased an Arabic language teacher’s jail term from six to 10 years and ordered him to be caned twice for sexually assaulting an eight-year-old pupil at a school in Muar, Johor, in 2019.

A three-member panel chaired by Justice Zaini Mazlan, sitting with Justices Ahmad Shahrir Salleh and Dean Wayne Daly, unanimously allowed the prosecution’s cross-appeal to enhance the sentence against Ahnaf Afiq Shairul Bazri, 35, while dismissing his appeal against conviction.

“The victim was only eight years old and the accused abused the position of trust placed in him as a teacher entrusted with the care and education of pupils. These are significant aggravating factors,” he said.
On Ahnaf’s appeal against his conviction, Zaini said the panel agreed with the High Court’s decision to set aside the acquittal and discharge granted by the Muar sessions court on March 19 last year.
He said the victim’s testimony was clear and detailed, and was supported by her immediate disclosure of the incident to her mother on the same day.
Ahnaf was charged with sexually assaulting the girl in a workroom at the library of a primary school in Muar between 10.20am and 11.20am on Oct 3, 2019.
Lawyers Radzi Yatiman and Nor Hafizah Abdullah represented Ahnaf, while deputy public prosecutor Aznin Ariff appeared for the prosecution.

442f153a87746f3d: LONDON: The UK's iconic Glastonbury Festival on Wednesday unveiled its 2027 line-up with top names Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Sam Fender, set to headline alongside veteran star Cher.
Tickets for the event next June sold out in 45 minutes last month with thousands rushing for sought-after places despite the hefty price tag.
Other big names on the bill include Massive Attack, Lily Allen, Lola Young, Kraftwerk, Texas and De La Soul, according to the line-up poster released on the festival's website.
Country star Kacey Musgraves, rising star FKA twigs and newcomer Adela also make the cut, with more acts still to be announced.
Cher, 80, will play the legend slot on Sunday. Aged 81 by the time she performs, she will be the oldest artist to do so, taking the crown from Rod Stewart.

The festival held at Worthy Farm in southwest England has become a fixture of the international musical calendar after first launching in 1970, inspired by British hippie and counterculture movements.
Prices have risen steadily in the last decade, with standard tickets costing £408 (US$539) for the June 2027 iteration, which follows the "fallow year" of no festival in 2026.
"We are so happy to be coming back after our fallow year," said organiser Emily Eavis on Instagram, describing the line-up as an "incredible" spread of artists.

Once a mecca for legendary British rockers, Glastonbury's line-up in recent years has veered to include global pop stars alongside festival veterans, with the likes of Charli XCX, Dua Lipa and Olivia Rodrigo gracing the stages.

The festival, popularly known as Glasto, courted controversy in 2025 after two acts offered messages of support for Palestinians in Gaza, where the UN says there are "reasonable grounds" to conclude that Israel's authorities and security forces "have continued to commit the crime of genocide".
Police assessed comments made on stage by Irish rappers Kneecap and the London-based duo Bob Vylan – but ultimately took no action against either band.
Frontman Bobby Vylan had led the crowd in chants against the Israeli army, sparking a backlash against the BBC from some quarters for its live broadcast of the moment.
Glastonbury 2025, attended by some 210,000 people, featured veteran stars Neil Young and Rod Stewart, as well as performances by Raye, The Prodigy, Alanis Morissette and Snow Patrol.

The festival also saw singer Lewis Capaldi make an emotional return to the vaunted Pyramid Stage, two years after he stopped a performance on the same stage as he struggled to overcome his Tourette's symptoms.
The 2027 festival will run from June 23 to 27.

35e286365003c0c5: KUALA LUMPUR: Kepercayaan awam merupakan aset paling bernilai bagi badan kehakiman dan mesti dilindungi melalui kebebasan kehakiman, keadilan serta ketelusan, kata Ketua Hakim Negara Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh.

Dalam syarahan di Universiti Sunway bertajuk 'Public Trust: The Judiciary’s Most Precious Constitutional Asset', beliau berkata kekuatan sebenar mahkamah bukan terletak pada kuasa atau bangunan yang gah, sebaliknya pada keyakinan rakyat terhadap keupayaan mahkamah menegakkan keadilan tanpa rasa takut atau pilih kasih.
"Kepercayaan awam terbit daripada keberanian tersebut, menerusi setiap penghakiman yang disampaikan secara telus tanpa rasa takut atau pilih kasih," katanya.

Wan Farid berkata kebebasan kehakiman adalah penting untuk melindungi rakyat daripada kuasa negara digunakan secara sewenang-wenang, menegaskan bahawa hakim mesti bebas daripada campur tangan politik dan hanya berpandukan perlembagaan serta undang-undang.

Merujuk kepada krisis kehakiman 1988 dan keputusan-keputusan bersejarah selepas itu, termasuk kes Semenyih Jaya, beliau berkata sejarah Malaysia membuktikan betapa mudahnya kepercayaan awam terhakis apabila kebebasan kehakiman dicurigai.

Beliau menegaskan keadilan bukan sahaja mesti ditegakkan, tetapi mesti disampaikan melalui tatacara yang adil, tanpa kelewatan yang tidak wajar, serta dalam bahasa yang boleh difahami oleh orang ramai.

Mengimbau ketika beliau berkhidmat sebagai hakim Mahkamah Tinggi di Kota Bharu, Kelantan, Wan Farid berkata beliau pernah perasan seorang tertuduh kelihatan terpinga-pinga ketika beliau membacakan penghakiman dalam bahasa Inggeris.
Tertuduh tersebut kemudiannya bertanya kepada peguamnya mengenai maksud sebenar keputusan berkenaan.
"Detik itu terus melekat dalam ingatan saya. Sejak hari itu, saya bertekad untuk menyampaikan penghakiman dalam bahasa yang jelas dan mudah difahami oleh pihak-pihak yang terlibat," katanya.
Wan Farid memberi amaran bahawa kepercayaan awam boleh terhakis secara beransur-ansur akibat kelewatan penghakiman, keputusan yang tidak dijelaskan, konflik kepentingan serta salah laku.

Beliau juga mengingatkan orang ramai agar tidak melakukan serangan dalam talian terhadap hakim dan keputusan mahkamah, sambil membezakan antara kritikan yang sah terhadap hujah perundangan dengan serangan peribadi yang bertujuan melemahkan keyakinan awam.
"Kami terbuka kepada kritikan, tetapi biarlah ia bersifat intelektual. Kritikan terhadap penaakulan undang-undang dan serangan terhadap badan kehakiman adalah dua perkara yang jauh berbeza," katanya.

Beliau menyeru hakim supaya bersikap terbuka terhadap penelitian, mengamalkan sikap rendah diri dan tekun, serta melayan setiap pihak yang berurusan di mahkamah dengan penuh kesabaran dan rasa hormat.
Mengakhiri syarahan dengan kisah 'Humpty Dumpty', beliau mengingatkan bahawa kepercayaan yang telah punah tidak mudah dipulihkan, walaupun dengan penggubalan undang-undang mahupun tindakan kerajaan.
"Kebebasan badan kehakiman mesti dipertahankan dengan tegas, sebelum kejatuhan benar-benar berlaku," katanya.

76d77bc28b54ae06: SHENZHEN: Malaysia is seeking clarification from the US on new restrictions governing artificial intelligence chips, particularly licensing requirements and the provision of data centre services to third parties, says investment, trade and industry minister Johari Ghani.

Johari said Malaysia was engaging with US authorities, including the US embassy and trade representatives, to obtain official details on the regulations and their implications for data centre operators in the country.
He said the government would inform the developers of all 117 approved data centre projects of the requirements once Washington has formally communicated them.
Some of the projects are already operational, while others are under construction.
He said operators seeking to acquire US-made graphics processing units (GPUs) for their data centres must comply with US regulations, including licensing requirements and due diligence procedures.

“If you want that GPU chip for your data centre that comes from the US, you have to comply with the US rules and regulations. Whoever is willing to comply, comply, then you can buy the chip,” he told Malaysian journalists on the sidelines of the Apec Economic Leaders' Week here today.

Johari said licensing requirements could be verified for buyers whose end-customers were US companies or hyperscalers. Transactions involving customers in other countries could require more extensive due diligence and know-your-customer checks by US authorities.
He said Malaysia did not manufacture the chips but facilitated data centre operations. As such, operators using US-made GPUs must comply with regulations governing the technology.

On allegations that Malaysia was being used as a transshipment hub for restricted AI chips, Johari said investigations were ongoing, but the government had yet to receive documentary evidence showing that data centre tenants had traded or re-exported the chips.
He said the authorities would check with the customs department to establish whether any GPUs had been re-exported, identify the parties involved, and examine shipping manifests and declarations.
“I have yet to see documentation that shows some of these players - the tenants who ran the data centres - traded the chips. I have not seen the documents yet.
“If they re-export, we want to know who, and they have to come up with the manifests they submitted. Only then can we proceed. We cannot simply accuse,” he said.
He said the investigation would establish whether such transactions had taken place, when they occurred, the quantities involved, and the parties responsible.

Johari said the US, as the chip manufacturer, should also conduct due diligence on buyers and inform Malaysia of companies intending to bring GPUs into the country for data centre operations, allowing local authorities to monitor their use.

He said Malaysia remained committed to ensuring that businesses operating in the country complied with relevant laws and regulations, including those imposed by other countries to protect intellectual property and strategic technologies.
Malaysia welcomed data centre investments, but their operators must comply with regulations governing the chips if they wanted to continue operating in the country.

“My advice to all data centre operators in Malaysia is, if you want to continue conducting your business here, you must comply with US rules and regulations. If you are not prepared to comply, then you should not operate in Malaysia,” he said.

He also said the new US restrictions would not necessarily undermine Malaysia’s attractiveness as an investment destination, but could affect operators who failed to comply, particularly their ability to secure customers.

He said Malaysia was also seeking clarification on restrictions covering the provision of data centre services, as the regulations appeared to extend beyond the physical re-export of GPUs to the use of computing capacity by third parties.

“We have not received anything from the US, other than what we have read in the media. This is where the communication will take place to ensure we have clear guidelines on the selling of GPU chips and the provision of data centre services,” he said.

On Monday, the Trump administration introduced new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres that allow Chinese companies to access advanced AI chips to train their artificial intelligence models.
The rules require companies in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil to apply for US export licences for the most advanced chips to prevent their illegal diversion.

7f054a92225181ea: The Home Office has awarded a contract worth £178 million to a public-private hosting services joint venture - without competition - to support critical national infrastructure.

According to a notice published last week, Crown Hosting Data Centres (CHDC) won the seven-year contract to support "essential national infrastructure underpinning the Home Office's most critical systems, including border security, the Police National Computer (PNC), and core intelligence environments."

CHDC is a joint venture between the Cabinet Office, which owns 25 percent, and Ark Data Centres Ltd, which owns the rest. It was set up in 2015 for the express purpose of providing hosting services for the government.
The award was made through an existing framework agreement, set up in February 2022, awarded to CHDC without competition via a Voluntary Ex-Ante Transparency Notice.
The service is set to support Critical National Infrastructure, although the notice does not reveal specific services requested.

Mention of continued support for the Police National Computer may raise eyebrows. The Home Office is managing the transition of the aging legacy system to the Law Enforcement Data Service (LEDS) under the National Law Enforcement Data Program (NLEDP).

A notice in December 2024 said that the Home Office was "focused on the development and adoption of LEDS products to replace existing PNC capability across all police forces and other non-policing PNC consumers, enabling the retirement by March 2026 (the point at which PNC support will expire)." The government had previously set a target of decommissioning the PNC in 2022.
The Register has asked the Home Office to clarify why Crown Hosting support is necessary beyond this date.
The PNC – which is based on mainframe technology dating from the 1970s – was at the center of a scandal in 2021 when a technology failure led to the loss of 413,000 records of evidence.

The incident, which left then Prime Minister Boris Johnson floundering in Parliament, was the result of a scripting error in code designed to weed out records to be deleted from the PNC, a system running on a Fujitsu BS2000/OSD SE700-30 mainframe-based at a datacenter in Hendon, London.
In 2022, the Cabinet Office awarded a contract worth up to £250 million to CHDC, also without outside competition. ®

2a320e6357c66bb2: With realism that defies belief, this vast game easily accommodates its trademark foulmouthed, OTT chaos – as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre In GTA VI, Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen. Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start. If you had been spying on me playing this game over the past few weeks you may well have caught me robbing banks, shooting up a weed farm or tearing along the highway at sunset blaring Bad Bunny on the in-game radio, but you might equally have caught me doing squats at the gym, shopping, assembling a coffee table or walking along the beach eating ice-cream. There is such a multiplicity of things on offer here that it is difficult to nail down what this game definitively is. Is it an interactive crime movie? A city simulator? A driving game? A sort of absurdly expansive version of The Sims in which the people you’re dressing up and looking after just happen to be professional criminals? It will be different for everyone – that is the beauty of it. For me, though, this game is about Jason and Lucia, the fugitive couple through whom you experience all that Leonida has to offer. Jason is muscular, handsome, ex-military, steady and unflappable, sincere but spare with words. Lucia has been boosting cars since the age of 14, has a wicked sense of humour and takes zero bullshit. (Lucia is the scarier one; I found myself turning much more quickly to violence when playing as her.) At the start, Lucia is incarcerated and Jason is making a go of things in the sunbeaten Keys, working for a dodgy guy down on the marina and renting a run-down house on stilts with a jetty round the back and a pet snake. When Lucia gets out of prison, the two of them try to make some kind of life for themselves – but before long they get caught up with the wrong people and have to flee the cosy life they’ve just started building. 5dc7ea8a58c79538: BARCELONA: Spanish World Cup winner Juan Mata retired from football on Wednesday at the age of 38.
The former Chelsea and Manchester United playmaker left Australian side Melbourne Victory in September.
"Sometimes, to love... is to let go. "Thanks, football," Mata wrote on social media as he announced his retirement.
Mata was part of the Spain squad that won the 2010 World Cup in South Africa and the 2012 European Championship.
The midfield maestro broke through at Valencia, where he won the Copa del Rey, before joining Chelsea in 2011.

Mata won the Champions League in 2012 with the London club, among other trophies, and later signed for Manchester United in 2014 before heading to Turkish club Galatasaray, Japanese side Vissel Kobe, Western Sydney Wanderers and finally Melbourne Victory.
"Football will never leave my life," added Mata on his website.
"There are so many ways to continue loving the game, so many ways to keep using it as a vehicle for development.
"I may stop playing professionally, but I will never stop being a footballer."
Mata remains involved with Melbourne Victory after taking a minority ownership stake in the club.
The Spaniard also has stakes in Formula One team Alpine and Major League Soccer club San Diego FC.
In 2017, Mata co-founded charity, Common Goal, donating at least 1% of his salary to good causes.

f4548d27014ca906: BEIJING: Chinese tech firm Tencent posted slower quarterly revenue growth on Wednesday, as the gaming and advertising giant pushes ahead with heavy investment in artificial intelligence.

It comes at a time of investor jitters about when the eye-watering amounts spent around the world on AI development will show returns -- shaky ground further jolted by an espionage scandal that has engulfed US chip giant Nvidia.
Shenzhen-based Tencent is the developer and operator of China's ubiquitous mega-app WeChat, and has also emerged in recent years as one of the country's top AI players.
Tencent said revenue during the third quarter of 2026 was 207.3 billion yuan (US$31.1 billion), up 8% year-on-year -- slowing from 11% in the previous quarter.
Quarterly revenue fell short of Bloomberg analyst estimates of 210.5 billion yuan.
Net profit for the quarter rose nearly 1%t on-year to 63.6 billion yuan, beating estimates of 57.6 billion yuan.
Bloomberg Intelligence analysts said ahead of the earnings announcement that Tencent faces "mounting AI investment costs".

"The company's sharpened focus on AI won't drive incremental earnings this year, with rising AI-related costs... set to put a drag on margin and cash flow, while it remains in a heightened investment mode," the analysts added.
Tencent, which owns the developer of massively popular eSports titles including "League of Legends", has sizeable operations in other areas from cloud computing to entertainment.
It has, along with fellow Chinese tech titans Baidu and Alibaba, stepped up spending on AI products in recent years.
Founder Pony Ma earlier this year likened Tencent's previous AI efforts to a "leaky" ship, adding: "We still hope the ship can sail faster."

661574ba3ab7772f: DHAKA: A petrol bomb has killed a political activist in the hometown of ousted Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina, police said Wednesday, as violence spread weeks before her planned return to the country.
Hasina, who fled to India in August 2024 after a student-led uprising ended her 15-year iron-fisted rule, has vowed to return in December despite facing a death sentence.
With tensions running high, violent attacks have hit Hasina's hometown and political stronghold of Gopalganj.
Raju Mollah, an activist with the governing Bangladesh Nationalist Party, was attacked and killed by a petrol bomb, senior police officer Md Shamsul Azam told AFP.

In separate incidents on Tuesday, a police station and a lawmaker's residence were set ablaze, officials said. At least seven police personnel were injured and eight vehicles damaged, according to spokeswoman Kamarum Munira.
Elsewhere in the country, a series of Molotov cocktail blasts and arson attacks have been reported in recent days.
While police have not identified suspects in the Gopalganj attacks, the government led by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party has blamed Hasina's banned Awami League party for the violence.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed told parliament on Tuesday that "setting fires is in their nature, burning people alive is in their nature."
He also accused Hasina's supporters of fuelling unrest in the garment sector, where workers have been protesting for higher wages since October.
"They are capitalising on workers' grievances," he said. "Some opportunists disguised as workers have infiltrated the labour unrest."
Hasina, 79, was sentenced to death in absentia last year after a Bangladeshi court convicted her of crimes against humanity over the deadly 2024 crackdown on protesters.
She has nevertheless promised to return in December and reiterated her vow in recent weeks, reviving hope among her supporters.
564ad01eadd027ab: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit ended lower against the greenback and other major and regional currencies on Wednesday, amid a hawkish US interest rate outlook.
At 6pm, the local currency fell to 4.1130/4.1180 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0915/4.0960.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Afzanizam Rashid said traders were still assessing the implications of monetary policy developments for 2026, with their immediate focus on the US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for Dec 8-9.
“I suppose traders are still digesting what it means for monetary policy in 2026, and for now the immediate attention is on December's FOMC meeting,” he told Bernama.

He said Malaysia’s latest third-quarter (3Q) 2026 gross domestic product growth came in higher than the advance estimate, bringing growth for the first nine months of the year to 5.6%, compared with 4.8% in the corresponding period last year.

“Against such a backdrop, we see scope for the overnight policy rate’s (OPR) upward adjustment by 25 basis points in early 2027. However, a deceleration in private consumption growth to 4.3% could put a hurdle to such a decision,” he added.

5b7b4b5e64b29525: WASHINGTON: Nasa's Voyager 1 probe, which has been travelling through space for nearly 50 years, hit a milestone distance of one light-day away from Earth on Wednesday.
Already the most distant man-made object in the universe, the spacecraft is now about 26 billion kilometres (16 billion miles) away, according to the US space agency.
That is the distance a particle of light can travel in 24 hours.
The historic feat is "the best illustration of just how vast space is", said Tiffany Kataria from Nasa.
"So much of what we dream about is travelling to other stellar systems," she told AFP.
"And it took Voyager 1 nearly 50 years to get to just the edge of our own solar system, let alone to only a light-day."
She pointed out that many exoplanetary systems, in comparison, are at least several light-years away.
Launched in 1977, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 are the only spacecraft to have reached interstellar space – the region beyond our solar system, which they continue to explore.
Messages sent from Earth take about 24 hours to reach Voyager 1, and just as long for teams on the ground to receive a response.
Both Voyager spacecraft carry "Golden Records" – 30-centimetre (12-inch), gold-plated copper discs intended to convey the story of our world to extraterrestrials.
Some of Voyager 1's equipment, such as cameras, have been remotely switched off to save power, but the probe continues to study invisible phenomena such as magnetic fields, Kataria said.
The data it collects allows researchers like her to study "the gas, the dust and other material that exists between stars, between our Sun and other stars".
Voyagers 1 and 2 have previously explored the outer solar system, which contains the giant planets Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

Images of Jupiter taken by Voyager 1 first revealed the existence of rings around the gas giant and helped scientists understand the "really extreme vortices and weather that take place in the atmosphere", Kataria said.
"You could find so many things that both of these spacecraft have really enabled in our understanding."
03692ec60cac1bbf: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”

“Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”

In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.

Wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko says, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.

A lot of the company’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.

Mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko says. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.)

The company also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.

Osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo launched, later gave the company a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.

But not everyone is convinced by the technology or the company’s big claims. Avery Gilbert, a smell scientist and author of What the Nose Knows, has been sharply critical of Osmo on his Substack, arguing that some of its marketing claims are undocumented, and that its patent filings still rely on human sensory panels and perfumers, rather than AI. “This heavy reliance on human sensory judgments seems odd for a company premised on super-cool AI,” he wrote in March. A representative for Osmo did not respond in time for publication.

Michael Schmuker, a former professor of neural computation at the University of Hertfordshire who has previously consulted for Osmo, says the company’s technology is an achievement. With colleagues, he created an open-source, reverse-engineered version of Osmo’s 2023 model, but it lacks the reams of data the company has collected since.

But even with all this smell data, Osmo may be missing some of the factors that make human olfaction unique, Schmuker says. “Smell is super complex. Context is very important for smell. The same molecule may evoke a different association depending on context,” he says. “[The smell of] a French cheese like Camembert is partly the same molecule as in used nappies. You don’t confuse the two because of the context.”

In a controlled setting like a fragrance lab, this lack of context may not matter so much. But it could have an impact if Osmo’s technology becomes, as Wiltschko suggests, the “olfactive channel” for AI world models. Imagine a machine that could sniff out spoilage in food on a production line, or detect tumors through smell the way dogs have been trained to do in pilot studies.
For that to happen, sensor technology will need to get a lot better, Schmuker says. The models will need to keep improving. Medical diagnostics is the biggest prize.

“There’s a lot of history of companies that have gone directly at that mountain peak and, unfortunately, not been successful, because it is very expensive and it is very difficult,” Wiltschko says. “So what we’re doing is building this foundation at the foothills of all these mountains. We’re sending expeditions up to the mountains, doing explorations, and basically smelling the whole world.”

0bbe03ed3a7069de: SAP's commercial terms could put its latest AI tools out of reach for many customers, particularly smaller businesses running a single ERP system, the new chair of its German-speaking user group has warned.

Thomas Henzler, appointed chair of DSAG last month, told The Register that Joule Studio 2.0 – SAP's upgraded platform for developing and deploying AI agents to automate business tasks – is a leap forward.
Yet DSAG, which represents SAP users in Germany, Switzerland, and Austria, remains in talks with the vendor about the commercial conditions attached to access.

In July 2023, CEO Christian Klein told investors that SAP's "newest innovations and capabilities" will only be delivered in the public or private cloud using RISE with SAP, the vendor's lift-shift-and-transform program launched with partners and cloud providers in early 2021. Customers running ERP software on-premises, or hosting it with a hyperscaler outside RISE, will miss out, he said.

However, in May this year, SAP appeared to perform a U-turn. It said on-premises customers could access Joule 2.0 if they commit to a cloud "journey" through RISE with SAP, changing their support and commercial arrangements while migration projects are still underway.

Henzler told The Reg: "There is a gap between the customer's reality and SAP's strategy for the autonomous enterprise. A lot of customers are still planning to migrate to S/4HANA, and now the question is, 'what do we have to do to use SAP AI, and what does it mean regarding the cloud strategy?'

"Now it's a completely new strategy, a new approach, and a new underlying technology. The question is, what does it mean for existing projects, S/4HANA migrations, cloud migrations and so on? Is it necessary to rethink all the projects? Is there a big shift in the technology and architectures?"
The DSAG chair said the biggest challenge in connecting legacy on-prem systems, such as ECC, to the new Joule suite is the commercial model.

"Access requires a substantial RISE commitment and a minimum cloud-to-on-premise maintenance ratio. In practice, this creates a problem for customers with only one ECC system. To meet the cloud threshold, they have to convert their entire on-premises maintenance into a cloud subscription, which defeats the purpose of an on-premises connector. Consequently, the model only works for large enterprises with multiple SAP ERP systems that can, for example, migrate one system after the other to unlock AI for the rest," he said.

"In the end, to get the benefit you have to start a RISE with SAP migration. Therefore, the connector doesn't make sense for the majority of SME customers. From my perspective, this approach works only for large customers with multiple ERP systems, for example, if they take one system, move it to the cloud, and then another one. Then they can use AI, because they reach the needed ratio to use the on-prem connector. That is more or less a commercial approach. We need a solution for all customers, independent of the commercials."

The Register asked SAP to respond to Henzler's concerns. A spokesperson said: "The offering separates a customer's commercial commitment to cloud ERP from the timing of its operational migration. Customers that meet the applicable commercial and technical requirements can use supported AI capabilities with eligible ECC or on-premises SAP S/4HANA systems while modernizing their landscape. Eligibility is not determined by the number of ERP instances and can therefore also extend to single-instance customers."

There are thousands of SAP ERP users worldwide, including some of the world's largest businesses. Despite efforts to get them onto the latest iteration – S/4HANA – and in the cloud, where the vendor promised it could gather a greater "share of wallet" from customers, there has been a dogged resistance to these complex and time-consuming migrations.

Gartner figures for Q4 2024 showed only 39 percent of worldwide ECC customers – from a total of 35,000 – had bought or subscribed to SAP S/4HANA licenses. More recently, The Reg uncovered that SAP was about €2 billion short of its target for getting customers off on-prem support.
Customers still running older ERP systems face pressure to embrace AI-supported automation. Whether SAP's terms help them do that – or simply help move them onto RISE – remains the question. ®

3bfa2d4b216e269c: SAN FRANCISCO: Scandal-hit Californian chip giant Nvidia said Tuesday it has stopped shipping artificial intelligence chips from its "Hopper" series to China, as scrutiny grows over Beijing's access to powerful US semiconductors.
Advanced Nvidia chips are the world's top hardware for training and running AI tools -- making them highly sensitive equipment in the tech race between Washington and Beijing.

Lucrative sales of Nvidia chips -- and allegations they are smuggled to China through third countries -- are in the spotlight after former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a woman whom some US officials reportedly suspect of spying for Beijing.
In the third quarter, "sales of licensed Hopper data centre products to China was US$2.4 billion," interim CEO Colette Kress told an earnings call Tuesday.
But "our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licensed Hopper data center products to China."
Kress did not give a reason for the decision.
Dilin Wu, a research strategist at Pepperstone, told AFP "the timing says quite a lot."

"We don't know exactly what prompted the decision to stop shipments, but it certainly looks like Nvidia is trying to draw a clearer line around its China business and reassure regulators that compliance comes first."
This year, the Trump administration began allowing limited sales of the flagship "H200" chip from Nvidia's "Hopper" series to China.
But US conditions have made it difficult for shipments to be approved, with Beijing also seen as reluctant to buy H200s as its homegrown chip industry gains momentum.
Washington still bans the export of Nvidia's even more advanced "Blackwell" and "Rubin" GPUs to China, citing security concerns as advanced AI has military applications.
Huang's affair with Alice Huang, a former director of a Singapore-based cloud computing company, has tanked Nvidia's market value.

Alice Huang, no relation to Jensen, previously led Megaspeed International -- a company under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese tech firms obtain Nvidia chips in violation of US export controls.
As the scandal deepens, the US moved Monday to close loopholes in those restrictions.

Its new rules aim to crack down on both chip smuggling to China and the large gray market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres full of high-end Nvidia chips in Southeast Asian countries.
Chandy Ye, a dual-qualified Hong Kong solicitor and mainland China lawyer, told AFP that the practical impact of Nvidia's decision to stop Hopper shipments to China would be limited.

"Chinese authorities have already been actively steering the domestic tech sector away from procuring H200s since January 2026, meaning the local ecosystem has long been adjusting to this decoupling," she said.

"The far more consequential development is the sweeping new interim rule from the US Commerce Department restricting remote access to advanced computing capabilities," which closes a "massive loophole."

43c6c4ac0068ccff: JAKARTA، Nov 18 — Indonesia’s central bank has raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to six per cent، a pre-emptive move aimed at stabilising the weakening rupiah and containing inflation amid heightened global economic uncertainty. Bank Indonesia (BI) Communications Department executive director Ramdan Denny Prakoso said the decision was made at the central bank’s two-day Board of Governors meeting which concluded on Wednesday. The meeting also saw the Deposit Facility rate raised by 25 basis points to 5.25 per cent and the Lending Facility rate by the same margin to 6.75 per cent. “The increase is a measure to further strengthen rupiah exchange rate stabilisation against the impact of rising global uncertainty، as well as a pre-emptive measure to keep inflation in 2026 and 2027 within the target range of 2.5 per cent، plus or minus one percentage point، ” he said in a statement on Wednesday. The latest increase marks BI’s first benchmark rate hike since June 18، when it raised the rate to 5.75 per cent، a level maintained for the following four months through October. Ramdan said the rupiah stood at Rp18,245 (RM4.11) against the US dollar on Tuesday، weakening 0.66 per cent from its end-October level، amid persistent global uncertainty and weak foreign investor sentiment in the domestic stock market. He said the central bank would continue directing monetary policy towards strengthening rupiah exchange rate stability while maintaining accommodative macroprudential measures to support lending to the real sector and preserve financial system stability. He said BI would also optimise foreign exchange intervention through offshore non-deliverable forward transactions، as well as spot and domestic non-deliverable forward transactions in the domestic market، alongside measures to strengthen banking liquidity. “Going forward، BI projects that the rupiah exchange rate will remain stable، supported by its commitment، attractive yields، inflation controlled within the target، and favourable domestic economic prospects، ” he said. Ramdan said global financial market volatility remained elevated due to continuing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East، growing political instability in Europe and expectations of further monetary tightening in the United States. He said BI expected global economic growth to remain weak at around 3.1 per cent in 2026، with inflation remaining elevated at approximately 4.6 per cent، prompting investors to reduce portfolio investments in emerging markets. d39ad68dec251893: UK MPs want a watchdog with the power to pull the plug on dangerous AI models, rather than leave the likes of OpenAI and Anthropic to decide when they've gone too far.

In a report shared with The Register ahead of publication on Wednesday, a parliamentary committee is calling for an AI Safety and Security Bill that would give a watchdog powers to intervene while models are still being developed.

It could halt high-risk training and testing, block deployments, or suspend AI services if the risks can't be contained. LLMs are trained on billions of learned parameters and so developers can't always predict what a model will do in every situation.

The recommendations come from Parliament's Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, which questioned researchers, former AI employees, and representatives from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, and Meta.

All four companies assured MPs they wouldn't release models they considered unsafe. The trouble is, they don't use the same yardstick for safety, and UK law doesn't generally require them to get an independent opinion before releasing anything.
"We cannot give today’s AI leaders unfettered freedom to behave like modern-day Dr Frankensteins, creating dangers beyond anyone’s control," said committee chair Liam Byrne MP.
Just as with aviation, pharma or nuclear safety, UK government want to rely on manufacturers' assurance alone, and want regulation.

"Our hearings exposed gaps in independent scrutiny, incident reporting and powers to stop unsafe systems. Once some models are released, they cannot reliably be recalled," added Byrne. "Protection must begin while systems are being built and tested."

The committee's report, Guardrails for Growth: Making AI Safe, identifies ten holes in Britain's approach to AI safety, including the lack of mandatory incident reporting, limited access for independent testers, and inadequate protections for whistleblowers.

The UK already has an AI Security Institute (AISI), which has made a name for itself testing some of the world's most powerful models, but its work depends on voluntary cooperation, and it has no authority to stop a company releasing a model that raises safety concerns.

MPs want AISI to continue its testing work while a separate regulator takes responsibility for enforcement. Developers of designated high-risk systems would have to provide evidence supporting their safety claims and give independent researchers access to examine them. Significant changes to a model's capabilities or safeguards would trigger further scrutiny.

Former AI employees also told MPs that raising safety concerns can come at a price. Restrictive contracts, commercial pressures, and financial disincentives can all discourage staff from speaking out, the committee heard. MPs want stronger legal protections for whistleblowers and compulsory reporting of AI incidents and near misses.

There's a fair bit of money riding on this, too. Using OECD productivity estimates, the committee calculates that AI could leave Britain's economy up to £400 billion larger over the next decade. It also sees an opportunity for the UK to make money from independently testing AI models, building on the expertise already established at AISI. MPs argue that stronger safeguards could encourage businesses, particularly smaller firms, to adopt the technology.

"AI firms must be required to substantiate their safety claims, independent experts must be able to scrutinize them, and a regulator must have the power to intervene when risks cannot be controlled," Byrne said. "Ministers, accountable to Parliament, must decide what risks the public should be asked to bear."

MPs want the new laws on the books in the next parliamentary session, and say Britain should use its turn at the G20 helm in 2027 to get other countries on board with tougher rules for AI testing, incident reporting, and risky model releases.

Whether ministers are prepared to hand a watchdog the power to stop AI development is another matter. The committee's recommendations aren't binding, and the government has yet to commit to the proposed legislation. ®
a38995cedd88a3d8: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has issued a statement calling on the relevant authorities to explain how the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting minutes that discussed Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s conditional pardon had been made public. The alleged copies of the meeting details are now being circulated on the internet, and first reported by news portal Malaysiakini. All documents related to the Pardons Board are official secrets, and there are processes to observe before it can be made public. Umno’s statement referred to the DAP’s Tony Pua as the source of the leaked minutes. “For documents with official secret status, the decision to declassify them must be made by the authority under Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act 1972 [Act 88] according to the applicable procedures,” said Azalina, who is also minister for law and institutional reforms. Malaysiakini said it had received the minutes from a well-placed source and alleged that the documents were declassified for court purposes, in response to the Bar Council’s legal challenge against the house arrest order. The documents do not appear to have been filed in court as of this morning, the portal noted. Umno said the “responsible parties” must provide an official explanation regarding its declassification status, if they have been declassified, when and by whom. Azalina also questioned the basis of authority and purpose of the purported declassification, and if circulating copies match the official record. “What is the basis of authority used, the procedure followed, and the purpose of the declassification? Does the declassification cover the entirety of the minutes, including related attachments, or only certain parts?” The minister asked. The alleged minutes detailed how FT Minister Hannah Yeoh and Attorney General Tan Sri Dusuki Mokhtar had opposed allowing Najib to serve the remaining jail sentence from his SRC International corruption conviction at home. Malaysiakini claimed Yeoh was also reluctant to sign off on the meeting. Najib is serving his prison sentence at home until August 2028 after he managed to pay the conditional RM50 million penalty.
12dd8e0a6a120bd3: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The impact of the latest United States (US) restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres is still too early to assess, as developments surrounding the matter are still unfolding, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour. He said BNM concurred with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry’s (Miti) stance that Malaysia would continue to engage with the relevant authorities on the matter. “This is one example where geo-economic risks are real and present, not just for us, but also for the rest of the world. “As far as Malaysia is concerned, as Miti has also stated, we will continue to uphold rules-based trade, remain open for business, and pursue our diversification strategy,” he said at the release of the third-quarter 2026 (3Q 2026) gross domestic product (GDP) data today. On Monday, the administration of US President Donald Trump issued a rule imposing new restrictions on chip exports to overseas data centres that enable Chinese companies to access advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips for training their AI models. The reports also stated that companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil would be required to obtain US export licences for the most advanced chips, as part of efforts to prevent their illegal diversion. Abdul Rasheed also emphasised that diversification remained a key strategy guiding Malaysia’s developments across various sectors, including date centres. He noted that of the 120 data centre companies operating in Malaysia, only 17, or about 13 per cent, were Chinese-owned, while the remainder originated from the US, Australia, Canada, and Malaysia. “This is where our investments (in data centres) are highly diversified. Therefore, the (US) restrictions are not expected to have a significant impact on data centre investments. “Based on our estimates of ongoing and planned projects, investment momentum in data centres is expected to remain strong at least until 2028,” he said, adding that sustained underlying demand for data centres would also create lasting economic linkages for Malaysia. According to Abdul Rasheed, the positive fundamentals are also consistent with the Malaysian Investment Development Authority’s (MIDA) approved information, communication and technology (ICT) investments, which increased to about RM38.9 billion in the first quarter of this year. **Impact of US midterm elections** Commenting on the US midterm election results, which could see the Democrats take control of Congress in January and increase scrutiny of the Trump administration’s tariff, data centre and AI policies, he said it was still too early to assess the potential implications for Malaysia’s economy as the situation continued to evolve. He stressed that strengthening the country’s economic fundamentals and foundations would help shield Malaysia from global developments and uncertainties. “On our part, we will continue to monitor the situation closely and assess its potential impact on the economy and financial markets, as well as the measures that we can put in place. “In addition, this is where buffers matter. That is why I always stress the importance of building up buffers during good times, when we are (in a) strong (position), so that we can always draw on them during difficult periods or in the event of unexpected developments,” he added. — Bernama
b5b42c8fd0be99c1: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 18 — The implementation of targeted fuel subsidies has not resulted in a significant increase in the prices of essential goods or public transport fares, based on monitoring by the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN). According to the ministry, the distribution of subsidies through the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) and Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) took into account their potential impact on the transportation costs of essential goods, land public transport fares, as well as ferry and passenger boat services. “Based on monitoring of essential goods prices and public transport fares, no significant price increases have been reported following the implementation of targeted fuel subsidies, which began on June 10, 2024, for SKDS and September 30, 2025, for SKPS,” the ministry said in a written reply published on the official Parliament website.
